title: Correlates of hepatitis B virus awareness and disease specific knowledge in Uganda: a meta-analysis and meta-regression of studies published between 2018 and 2025
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major public health challenge in Uganda, where prevalence varies by region and population group despite national vaccination and screening initiatives. Understanding awareness and knowledge levels is essential for guiding HBV prevention and control strategies. This study synthesized available evidence on the correlates of HBV awareness and disease specific knowledge among different Ugandan populations. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, African Journals Online (AJOL), and Google Scholar for cross-sectional studies reporting on HBV awareness or disease-specific knowledge in Uganda, published between January 2018 and December 2025. Study selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal were conducted independently by two reviewers using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-Sectional Studies. Eighteen studies meeting the eligibility criteria were included in the final synthesis. Pooled estimates of HBV awareness and correlates of disease-specific knowledge were computed using a random-effects model in MedCalc software (version 10.10), with heterogeneity quantified using the I2 statistic. Sources of heterogeneity were explored through subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis. Meta-regression was performed to examine trends in HBV awareness by region, year of publication, and study population. Publication bias was assessed using Begg's and Egger's tests. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, and all estimates are reported with 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of HBV awareness was 75.3% (95% CI: 61.5%-86.9%), with substantial heterogeneity observed across regions and population groups (I2=99.24%). Subgroup analysis revealed that awareness was significantly higher in Central Uganda compared to the northern, eastern, and western regions (p < 0.05), and among healthcare workers compared to the general population and antenatal care attendees (p < 0.05). Knowledge of specific HBV domains varied considerably: awareness of the causative agent, screening services, and vaccination availability was significantly higher among knowledgeable participants compared to those with no prior HBV knowledge (p < 0.05), whereas awareness of post-exposure prophylaxis and completion of the full HBV vaccination schedule remained low compared to those who had received at least partial vaccination (p < 0.05). Awareness of key transmission routes including sexual contact, needle sharing, and mother-to-child transmission was moderate, though knowledge of transmission through infected body fluids remained poor. Participants who were of higher education level were more likely to take up vaccination compared to lower education level (p < 0.05), and participants with a positive attitude toward vaccine effectiveness were significantly more likely to be vaccinated compared to those with a negative attitude (p < 0.05). The meta-regression analysis further revealed a paradoxical overall decline in HBV awareness over the study period. CONCLUSION: Critical gaps still persist in HBV awareness and key knowledge areas highlighting the need for alternative strategies tailored to the social dynamics of the current generation during the delivery of health messages. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管采取了疫苗接种和筛查举措,乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 仍然是乌干达的一个主要公共卫生挑战,了解意识和知识水平对于指导预防和控制策略至关重要。这项研究综合了乌干达人群对乙肝病毒的认识和特定疾病知识之间的相关性证据,以解决目前认识上的差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们进行了系统回顾和荟萃分析,综合了 2018 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间 PubMed、非洲期刊在线和 Google Scholar 发表的横断面研究。经过独立选择、数据提取和两名评审员使用乔安娜·布里格斯研究所批判性评估清单进行质量评估后,纳入了十八项研究。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 MedCalc 软件中的随机效应模型计算 HBV 认知度和特定疾病知识相关性的汇总估计,并使用 I2 统计量量化异质性。元回归检查了按地区、出版年份和研究人群划分的趋势,并使用 Begg 和 Egger 检验评估了发表偏倚。
elements_zh.main_results: 乙型肝炎知晓率汇总为 75.3%(95% CI:61.5%-86.9%),存在显着异质性(I2=99.24%)。乌干达中部地区的意识显着高于北部、东部和西部地区,医护人员的意识也明显高于普通民众和产前护理人员。在暴露后预防和完成完整乙肝疫苗接种计划方面仍然存在知识差距。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究突显了乙型肝炎意识和关键知识领域的严重差距,特别是在传播途径和疫苗接种计划方面,尽管总体意识较高。它指出随着时间的推移,人们对乙肝病毒的认识出现了矛盾的下降,并强调需要制定量身定制的策略来解决健康信息传递中的社会动态问题。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果通过确定区域和特定人群在意识和知识方面的差异,指导医护人员、产前护理人员和教育弱势群体的干预措施,为有针对性的乙肝预防和控制策略提供信息。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major public health challenge in Uganda despite vaccination and screening initiatives, and understanding awareness and knowledge levels is essential for guiding prevention and control strategies. This study synthesized evidence on correlates of HBV awareness and disease-specific knowledge among Ugandan populations to address gaps in current understanding.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted, synthesizing cross-sectional studies published between January 2018 and December 2025 from PubMed, African Journals Online, and Google Scholar. Eighteen studies were included after independent selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal by two reviewers using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist.
analysis_en.methods: Pooled estimates of HBV awareness and correlates of disease-specific knowledge were computed using a random-effects model in MedCalc software, with heterogeneity quantified using the I2 statistic. Meta-regression examined trends by region, publication year, and study population, and publication bias was assessed using Begg's and Egger's tests.
analysis_en.main_results: The pooled prevalence of HBV awareness was 75.3% (95% CI: 61.5%-86.9%), with substantial heterogeneity (I2=99.24%). Awareness was significantly higher in Central Uganda than in northern, eastern, and western regions, and among healthcare workers compared to the general population and antenatal care attendees. Knowledge gaps persisted in post-exposure prophylaxis and completion of the full HBV vaccination schedule.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights critical gaps in HBV awareness and key knowledge areas, particularly in transmission routes and vaccination schedules, despite high overall awareness. It identifies a paradoxical decline in HBV awareness over time and emphasizes the need for tailored strategies to address social dynamics in health messaging.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform targeted HBV prevention and control strategies by identifying regional and population-specific disparities in awareness and knowledge, guiding interventions for healthcare workers, antenatal care attendees, and educationally disadvantaged groups.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by substantial heterogeneity across studies and regions, and the meta-regression revealed a paradoxical decline in awareness over time, which may reflect reporting bias or changing study populations rather than true trends. The overall strength of evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

title_zh: 乌干达乙型肝炎病毒认识与疾病特定知识的相关性:对 2018 年至 2025 年发表的研究进行荟萃分析和荟萃回归
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major public health challenge in Uganda, where prevalence varies by region and population group despite national vaccination and screening initiatives. Understanding awareness and knowledge levels is essential for guiding HBV prevention and control strategies. This study synthesized available evidence on the correlates of HBV awareness and disease specific knowledge among different Ugandan populations. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, African Journals Online (AJOL), and Google Scholar for cross-sectional studies reporting on HBV awareness or disease-specific knowledge in Uganda, published between January 2018 and December 2025. Study selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal were conducted independently by two reviewers using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-Sectional Studies. Eighteen studies meeting the eligibility criteria were included in the final synthesis. Pooled estimates of HBV awareness and correlates of disease-specific knowledge were computed using a random-effects model in MedCalc software (version 10.10), with heterogeneity quantified using the I2 statistic. Sources of heterogeneity were explored through subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis. Meta-regression was performed to examine trends in HBV awareness by region, year of publication, and study population. Publication bias was assessed using Begg's and Egger's tests. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, and all estimates are reported with 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of HBV awareness was 75.3% (95% CI: 61.5%-86.9%), with substantial heterogeneity observed across regions and population groups (I2=99.24%). Subgroup analysis revealed that awareness was significantly higher in Central Uganda compared to the northern, eastern, and western regions (p < 0.05), and among healthcare workers compared to the general population and antenatal care attendees (p < 0.05). Knowledge of specific HBV domains varied considerably: awareness of the causative agent, screening services, and vaccination availability was significantly higher among knowledgeable participants compared to those with no prior HBV knowledge (p < 0.05), whereas awareness of post-exposure prophylaxis and completion of the full HBV vaccination schedule remained low compared to those who had received at least partial vaccination (p < 0.05). Awareness of key transmission routes including sexual contact, needle sharing, and mother-to-child transmission was moderate, though knowledge of transmission through infected body fluids remained poor. Participants who were of higher education level were more likely to take up vaccination compared to lower education level (p < 0.05), and participants with a positive attitude toward vaccine effectiveness were significantly more likely to be vaccinated compared to those with a negative attitude (p < 0.05). The meta-regression analysis further revealed a paradoxical overall decline in HBV awareness over the study period. CONCLUSION: Critical gaps still persist in HBV awareness and key knowledge areas highlighting the need for alternative strategies tailored to the social dynamics of the current generation during the delivery of health messages. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.
abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)仍然是乌干达的一个主要公共卫生挑战,尽管国家采取了疫苗接种和筛查举措,但其患病率因地区和人群而异。了解意识和知识水平对于指导乙肝预防和控制策略至关重要。这项研究综合了乌干达不同人群对乙肝病毒的认识和疾病具体知识之间的相关性的现有证据。方法:我们系统地检索了 PubMed、非洲期刊在线 (AJOL) 和 Google Scholar,查找 2018 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间发表的关于乌干达 HBV 认知或特定疾病知识的横断面研究。研究选择、数据提取和质量评估由两名评审员使用 Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) 分析横断面研究批判评估清单独立进行。最终综合报告中纳入了十八项符合资格标准的研究。使用 MedCalc 软件(版本 10.10)中的随机效应模型计算 HBV 认知度和特定疾病知识相关性的汇总估计,并使用 I2 统计量量化异质性。通过亚组分析和敏感性分析探讨异质性的来源。进行元回归以检查按地区、出版年份和研究人群划分的 HBV 认知趋势。使用 Begg 和 Egger 测试评估发表偏倚。统计显着性设置为 p < 0.05,所有估计值均以 95% 置信区间报告。结果:十八项研究符合纳入标准。乙型肝炎知晓率汇总率为 75.3%(95% CI:61.5%-86.9%),不同地区和人群之间存在显着异质性(I2=99.24%)。亚组分析显示,与北部、东部和西部地区相比,乌干达中部地区的知晓率显着较高(p < 0.05),与一般人群和产前护理人员相比,医护人员的知晓率显着较高(p < 0.05)。对特定 HBV 领域的了解差异很大:与先前没有 HBV 知识的参与者相比,知识丰富的参与者对病原体、筛查服务和疫苗接种可用性的认识显着较高 (p < 0.05),而与至少接受部分疫苗接种的参与者相比,对暴露后预防和完成完整 HBV 疫苗接种计划的认识仍然较低 (p < 0.05)。尽管对通过受感染体液传播的了解仍然很少,但对性接触、共用针头和母婴传播等关键传播途径的了解程度较低。与教育水平较低的参与者相比,受教育程度较高的参与者更有可能接种疫苗(p < 0.05),对疫苗有效性持积极态度的参与者比持消极态度的参与者更有可能接种疫苗(p < 0.05)。荟萃回归分析进一步揭示了研究期间乙肝病毒认知度整体下降的矛盾现象。结论:对乙肝病毒的认识和关键知识领域仍然存在严重差距,这突出表明在传播健康信息时需要针对当代社会动态制定替代策略。临床试验编号:不适用。

title: Trends in Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV Seroprevalence in the Netherlands: Insights From Two Decades of Nationwide PIENTER Serosurveys
abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C (HCV), and HIV remain public health challenges despite effective treatments and preventive options. Infections are often asymptomatic, leading to undiagnosed cases, onward transmission, and preventable morbidity and mortality. In the Netherlands, disease burden is concentrated in specific populations, with many undetected infections. We estimated HBV, HCV, and HIV seroprevalence, identified determinants, and assessed trends over 20 years using data from 14,444 participants aged 15–79 years from three nationwide cross‐sectional serosurveys (PIENTER: 1995–1996, 2006–2007, and 2016–2017). Participants completed questionnaires on demographics, behaviour, and socio‐economic factors, and serum samples were tested for HBV and HCV in all rounds and HIV in 2017. Seroprevalence estimates were weighted to the Dutch population, trends were analysed using weighted Poisson regression, and determinants were evaluated using multivariable Poisson regression. Weighted HBV seroprevalence remained stable across surveys (3%–5% past or present infection; < 0.4% active infection). HBV prevalence was highest among first‐generation migrants, with older age, migration background, and STI history as key determinants. HCV seroprevalence remained low (< 0.4%) and was highest among non‐Western migrants. HIV prevalence was 0.1% and highest among non‐Western migrants and men who have sex with men. Only 9% of active HBV cases were aware of their status. Overall, HBV, HCV, and HIV seroprevalence remain low in the Netherlands but are concentrated in specific groups with limited awareness. These findings support targeted prevention, screening, and linkage‐to‐care strategies to achieve the 2030 WHO elimination goals and highlight the importance of continued population‐based (sero‐)monitoring to guide public health policy.
authors: Christine G. J. I. van Straten
Fiona R. M. van der Klis
Eline L. M. Op de Coul

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in the Netherlands, focusing on seroprevalence trends, determinants, and population-level burden over two decades among individuals aged 15–79 years, with a central question on identifying high-risk groups and informing targeted public health strategies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes data from three nationwide cross-sectional serosurveys (PIENTER: 1995–1996, 2006–2007, 2016–2017) involving 14,444 participants, using weighted seroprevalence estimates, Poisson regression for trend analysis, and multivariable regression to assess determinants, with serum samples tested for HBV and HCV in all rounds and HIV in 2017.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HBV, HCV, and HIV seroprevalence in the Netherlands remain low overall (< 0.4% for HCV and HIV; 3%–5% for past or present HBV infection), with stable trends over 20 years, but highlights concentrated burden in specific groups such as first-generation migrants, non-Western migrants, and men who have sex with men, alongside low awareness of active HBV infection (9%).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies limited awareness of active HBV infection as a critical evidence gap, with only 9% of cases aware of their status, and notes that the low overall prevalence contrasts with the high burden in specific populations, suggesting potential underdiagnosis or underreporting in these groups.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for targeted prevention, screening, and linkage-to-care strategies to achieve WHO 2030 elimination goals, and underscores the importance of continued population-based seromonitoring to guide public health policy and resource allocation.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes two decades of nationwide serosurvey data (PIENTER) from 14,444 Dutch participants aged 15–79 years to assess trends in hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV seroprevalence. Weighted estimates and regression analyses reveal stable low prevalence overall (< 0.4% for HCV/HIV; 3%–5% for HBV past/present infection), with concentrated burden in first-generation migrants, non-Western migrants, and men who have sex with men. Only 9% of active HBV cases are aware of their status, highlighting a critical gap in diagnosis. The review concludes that targeted prevention and screening are essential to meet WHO elimination targets and calls for sustained seromonitoring to inform policy.

title: Serum M2BPGi as a predictor of hepatocellular carcinoma development in chronic hepatitis B and C: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) kills about 830,000 people each year, and most cases arise in chronic viral hepatitis. Better risk markers would let clinicians focus surveillance where it matters. Mac-2 binding protein glycosylation isomer (M2BPGi) is a serum glycobiomarker of liver fibrosis. Several cohort studies tie elevated M2BPGi to HCC. No quantitative synthesis has pooled this evidence across viral etiologies. Methods We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus through April 2026 for longitudinal studies that reported hazard ratios (HRs) for HCC linked to elevated M2BPGi in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) or C (HCV). We registered the protocol with PROSPERO. The primary pool restricted to longitudinal studies with categorical cutoffs that reported HRs. We used random-effects meta-analysis with restricted maximum likelihood and the Hartung–Knapp adjustment. Results Twenty-three publications (24 study entries) met inclusion criteria. The primary pool of 15 longitudinal categorical HR-reporting studies covered 12,161 participants and at least 1,189 HCC events. The pooled HR was 4.61 (95% CI 3.24–6.54; p < 0.0001) with low heterogeneity (I 2 = 25.6%). The 95% prediction interval ran from 2.08 to 10.18. The effect held across etiology (CHB k = 5 HR 4.12; HCV k = 10 HR 5.07; p_subgroup = 0.62) and across measurement timing (baseline HR 3.21; on/post-treatment HR 5.62; post-SVR HR 5.45; p_subgroup = 0.23). Two sensitivity pools re-introducing OR-based studies gave HR 4.71 ( k = 16) and HR 4.89 ( k = 17). Egger’s test was positive ( p = 0.0003); trim-and-fill imputed six studies and pulled the adjusted HR to 3.53. Conclusion Elevated serum M2BPGi is strongly and consistently associated with HCC development in patients with chronic hepatitis B and C. The effect holds across etiology, treatment status, and measurement timing–including after sustained virological response. Funnel asymmetry suggests the true effect is closer to a 3.5-fold than a 4.6-fold risk increase, still large enough to matter clinically. M2BPGi is a credible candidate to layer onto current viral hepatitis surveillance, particularly for risk stratification after virological control. analysis.scope_and_question: The review investigates the association between serum Mac-2 binding protein glycosylation isomer (M2BPGi) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) or C (HCV).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal cohort studies. The authors searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus through April 2026. Eligible studies reported hazard ratios (HRs) for HCC linked to elevated M2BPGi in CHB or HCV. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO. The analysis utilized random-effects meta-analysis with restricted maximum likelihood and the Hartung–Knapp adjustment.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Twenty-three publications (24 study entries) were included, with a primary pool of 15 longitudinal categorical HR-reporting studies covering 12,161 participants and at least 1,189 HCC events. The pooled hazard ratio for elevated M2BPGi was 4.61 (95% CI 3.24–6.54; p < 0.0001) with low heterogeneity (I2 = 25.6%). The association was consistent across viral etiologies (CHB HR 4.12; HCV HR 5.07) and measurement timing (baseline HR 3.21; on/post-treatment HR 5.62; post-SVR HR 5.45).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Funnel asymmetry was detected (Egger’s test p = 0.0003), suggesting publication bias. Trim-and-fill imputation adjusted the pooled HR to 3.53, indicating the true effect may be closer to a 3.5-fold risk increase than the initial estimate of 4.6-fold.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: M2BPGi is a credible candidate for integration into current viral hepatitis surveillance programs, particularly for risk stratification after achieving sustained virological response.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 study entries from 23 publications evaluates serum M2BPGi as a predictor of hepatocellular carcinoma in chronic hepatitis B and C. The analysis of 15 primary longitudinal studies involving over 12,000 participants found a strong association, with a pooled hazard ratio of 4.61 (95% CI 3.24–6.54). The effect was consistent across viral etiologies and measurement timing, including after sustained virological response. However, funnel asymmetry and trim-and-fill analysis suggest the true risk increase may be closer to 3.5-fold. The authors conclude that M2BPGi is a credible marker for risk stratification in surveillance programs.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述调查了慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 或丙型肝炎 (HCV) 患者血清 Mac-2 结合蛋白糖基化异构体 (M2BPGi) 与肝细胞癌 (HCC) 发展之间的关联。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是对纵向队列研究的系统回顾和荟萃分析。作者检索了截至 2026 年 4 月的 PubMed/MEDLINE、Embase、Cochrane 图书馆、Web of Science 和 Scopus。符合条件的研究报告了 HCC 的风险比 (HR) 与 CHB 或 HCV 中 M2BPGi 升高相关。该协议已在 PROSPERO 注册。该分析利用限制最大似然的随机效应荟萃分析和 Hartung-Knapp 调整。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 其中包括 23 篇出版物(24 项研究条目),其中主要有 15 项纵向分类 HR 报告研究,涵盖 12,161 名参与者和至少 1,189 个 HCC 事件。M2BPGi 升高的汇总风险比为 4.61(95% CI 3.24-6.54;p < 0.0001),异质性较低(I2 = 25.6%)。这种关联在病毒病因(CHB HR 4.12;HCV HR 5.07)和测量时间(基线 HR 3.21;治疗中/治疗后 HR 5.62;SVR 后 HR 5.45)方面是一致的。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 检测到漏斗不对称性(Egger 检验 p = 0.0003),表明存在发表偏倚。修剪填充插补将合并 HR 调整为 3.53,表明真实效果可能比最初估计的 4.6 倍更接近风险增加 3.5 倍。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: M2BPGi 是纳入当前病毒性肝炎监测计划的可靠候选者,特别是在实现持续病毒学应答后进行风险分层。

title: Spatiotemporal epidemiology of hepatitis B in Central China: urbanization drivers and implications for adult-targeted control strategies.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a significant global public health challenge. Hubei Province, a historically high-prevalence area in central China, continues to face persistently high rates of adult HBsAg carriers despite effective reduction of childhood transmission through universal vaccination, hindering progress toward HBV elimination goals. This study aims to identify key drivers behind the rising hepatitis B incidence in the region, forecast future trends, and inform targeted control strategies. METHODS: This population-based spatiotemporal epidemiological study analyzed hepatitis B surveillance data from Hubei Province between January 2015 and December 2024, covering 631,361 reported cases across 17 prefecture-level divisions. Spatial clustering was assessed using Global Moran's I statistics. Urbanization-related spatial drivers were identified via geographically weighted random forest modeling with SHAP value interpretation, and future incidence trends were predicted using Holt-Winters time series forecasting. RESULTS: The average annual incidence was 106.19 per 100,000 population, showing a U-shaped temporal trend: declining from 111.75 per 100,000 in 2015 to 83.58 in 2020, then rising to 125.86 in 2024. Adults aged 30-50 years consistently accounted for 40-50% of total cases. Significant spatial clustering was detected (Global Moran's I: 0.124-0.307, P < 0.05), with persistent high-risk zones concentrated in the Wuhan metropolitan area. The geographically weighted random forest model identified urbanization rate as the primary spatial driver (SHAP value ≈2.0), followed by higher education enrollment rate (≈1.0) and passenger traffic volume (≈0.8). Time series forecasting projected monthly incidence rates of 8.98-10.41 per 100,000 over the subsequent 18 months (R2 = 0.892, MAPE = 1.74%). CONCLUSION: In Hubei Province, the hepatitis B burden has concentrated in adults born before the vaccine era, underscoring horizontal transmission risks in this susceptible cohort. Urbanization significantly impacts the spatial distribution of hepatitis B, with high-risk areas mainly concentrated in the Wuhan metropolitan region. It is crucial to address urbanization-related factors affecting HBV transmission and to implement targeted screening and revaccination for adults aged 30-50, particularly among high-risk individuals, mobile populations, and rural residents, to reduce incidence and alleviate the regional disease burden.

This study aims to identify key drivers behind the rising hepatitis B incidence in the region, forecast future trends, and inform targeted control strategies. METHODS This population-based spatiotemporal epidemiological study analyzed hepatitis B surveillance data from Hubei Province between January 2015 and December 2024, covering 631,361 reported cases across 17 prefecture-level divisions. Spatial clustering was assessed using Global Moran's I statistics. Urbanization-related spatial drivers were identified via geographically weighted random forest modeling with SHAP value interpretation, and future incidence trends were predicted using Holt-Winters time series forecasting. RESULTS The average annual incidence was 106.19 per 100,000 population, showing a U-shaped temporal trend: declining from 111.75 per 100,000 in 2015 to 83.58 in 2020, then rising to 125.86 in 2024. Adults aged 30-50 years consistently accounted for 40-50% of total cases. Significant spatial clustering was detected (Global Moran's I: 0.124-0.307, P < 0.05), with persistent high-risk zones concentrated in the Wuhan metropolitan area. The geographically weighted random forest model identified urbanization rate as the primary spatial driver (SHAP value ≈2.0), followed by higher education enrollment rate (≈1.0) and passenger traffic volume (≈0.8). Time series forecasting projected monthly incidence rates of 8.98-10.41 per 100,000 over the subsequent 18 months (R2 = 0.892, MAPE = 1.74%). CONCLUSION In Hubei Province, the hepatitis B burden has concentrated in adults born before the vaccine era, underscoring horizontal transmission risks in this susceptible cohort. Urbanization significantly impacts the spatial distribution of hepatitis B, with high-risk areas mainly concentrated in the Wuhan metropolitan region. It is crucial to address urbanization-related factors affecting HBV transmission and to implement targeted screening and revaccination for adults aged 30-50, particularly among high-risk individuals, mobile populations, and rural residents, to reduce incidence and alleviate the regional disease burden.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管通过疫苗接种减少了儿童传播,但乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染仍然是中国中部湖北省的一个重大公共卫生挑战,而成人 HBsAg 携带率持续较高,阻碍了消除目标。这项研究旨在确定乙型肝炎发病率上升的驱动因素,预测未来趋势,并为有针对性的控制策略提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项基于人群的时空流行病学研究分析了湖北省2015年1月至2024年12月的乙型肝炎监测数据,覆盖17个地级市的631,361例报告病例。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 Global Moran's I 统计数据评估空间聚类,通过具有 SHAP 值解释的地理加权随机森林模型确定与城市化相关的空间驱动因素,并使用 Holt-Winters 时间序列预测预测未来的发病趋势。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究将乙型肝炎负担集中在疫苗时代之前出生的成年人中,强调了这一易感人群的水平传播风险。新颖之处在于使用地理加权随机森林模型将城市化率量化为乙肝病毒分布的主要空间驱动因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持对30-50岁的成年人,特别是在武汉等高风险城市地区、流动人口和农村居民进行有针对性的筛查和重新接种,以降低发病率并减轻区域乙肝负担。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于监测数据,可能会漏报病例,并且缺乏个体层面的风险因素数据,从而限制了因果推断。尽管有强大的时空模型,但由于监测系统和预测假设的潜在偏差,证据强度中等。

title: Texture Analysis of Non-contrast Magnetic Resonance Imaging for Liver Fibrosis Staging in Patients with Chronic Hepatitis B
abstract: Background and Aims: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of texture analysis parameters obtained from non-contrast liver magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in staging liver fibrosis in patients with chronic hepatitis B. Methods: Non-contrast MRI examinations of 66 patients with chronic hepatitis B were retrospectively evaluated. The protocol included in-phase T1-weighted (IP-T1W), out-of-phase T1-weighted (OP-T1W), fat-suppressed T1-weighted (FS-T1W), fat-suppressed T2-weighted (FS-T2W), and T2-weighted (T2W) sequences. Histogram-based texture features were extracted from regions of interest placed in the liver parenchyma. For each sequence, the most informative features were selected from 20 candidate variables using the minimal-redundancy maximal-relevance (mRMR) algorithm, and multivariable logistic regression models were constructed. Fibrosis was categorized as early fibrosis (F0-F2) or significant fibrosis (F3-F6). Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and area under the curve (AUC), and model generalizability was evaluated by 10-fold cross-validation. Results: Sixty-six patients were included (early fibrosis, n=43; significant fibrosis, n=23). ROC analysis showed that the highest discriminatory performance was obtained with the OP-T1W sequence (AUC=0.789, 95%CI: 0.677-0.900, p 0.05). Based on the Youden index-derived thresholds, the OP-T1W sequence achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (72.31%) and sensitivity (79.17%), whereas the FS-T1W sequence demonstrated the highest specificity (83.72%). In 10-fold cross-validation, the highest mean AUC was observed for OP-T1W (0.785±0.168), followed by FS-T2W (0.760±0.168), whereas IP-T1W showed a lower mean AUC (0.653±0.128). Conclusions: Texture analysis parameters derived from routine non-contrast MRI sequences in patients with chronic hepatitis B may provide additional quantitative information for the noninvasive assessment of liver fibrosis. These findings suggest that texture analysis may serve as a complementary tool within routine liver MRI. However, given the single-center design and limited sample size of the present study, further studies with larger cohorts and external validation are needed before clinical application.

The protocol included in-phase T1-weighted (IP-T1W), out-of-phase T1-weighted (OP-T1W), fat-suppressed T1-weighted (FS-T1W), fat-suppressed T2-weighted (FS-T2W), and T2-weighted (T2W) sequences. Histogram-based texture features were extracted from regions of interest placed in the liver parenchyma. For each sequence, the most informative features were selected from 20 candidate variables using the minimal-redundancy maximal-relevance (mRMR) algorithm, and multivariable logistic regression models were constructed. Fibrosis was categorized as early fibrosis (F0-F2) or significant fibrosis (F3-F6). Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and area under the curve (AUC), and model generalizability was evaluated by 10-fold cross-validation. RESULTS: Sixty-six patients were included (early fibrosis, n=43; significant fibrosis, n=23). ROC analysis showed that the highest discriminatory performance was obtained with the OP-T1W sequence (AUC=0.789, 95%CI: 0.677-0.900, p 0.05). Based on the Youden index-derived thresholds, the OP-T1W sequence achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (72.31%) and sensitivity (79.17%), whereas the FS-T1W sequence demonstrated the highest specificity (83.72%). In 10-fold cross-validation, the highest mean AUC was observed for OP-T1W (0.785±0.168), followed by FS-T2W (0.760±0.168), whereas IP-T1W showed a lower mean AUC (0.653±0.128). CONCLUSIONS: Texture analysis parameters derived from routine non-contrast MRI sequences in patients with chronic hepatitis B may provide additional quantitative information for the noninvasive assessment of liver fibrosis. These findings suggest that texture analysis may serve as a complementary tool within routine liver MRI. However, given the single-center design and limited sample size of the present study, further studies with larger cohorts and external validation are needed before clinical application.

title: Quality of life and self-reported stigma following hepatitis B surface antigen loss: A multi-site study by the Canadian Hepatitis B Network
abstract: Abstract Background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) imposes adverse health outcomes but may also cause psychosocial and quality-of-life (QOL) challenges. Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss, whether spontaneous or due to treatment (ie, a functional cure), is associated with improved clinical outcomes, but the impact of HBsAg clearance on patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) is poorly understood. Methods: Two surveys (hepatitis B self-stigma and hepatitis B–related QOL [HBQOL]) were administered to adults with a history of CHB with documented HBsAg clearance from six Canadian hepatology clinics. Results: Eighty-four participants were enrolled (median age: 60 years; 53.6% male). Nearly three quarters (72.6%) of patients reported never feeling self-stigma. HBQOL scores improved across all six domains ( p < 0.001 for each), with the largest relative gains in psychological well-being (60% reduction), transmission concerns (55%), and stigma (53%). Conclusions: HBsAg loss was associated with significant improvements in patient-reported stigma and QOL. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating PROMs into hepatitis B virus clinical care to better capture treatment experiences.

title_zh: 乙型肝炎表面抗原丧失后的生活质量和自我报告的耻辱:加拿大乙型肝炎网络的多中心研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) imposes adverse health outcomes but may also cause psychosocial and quality-of-life (QOL) challenges. Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss, whether spontaneous or due to treatment (ie, a functional cure), is associated with improved clinical outcomes, but the impact of HBsAg clearance on patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) is poorly understood. Methods: Two surveys (hepatitis B self-stigma and hepatitis B–related QOL [HBQOL]) were administered to adults with a history of CHB with documented HBsAg clearance from six Canadian hepatology clinics. Results: Eighty-four participants were enrolled (median age: 60 years; 53.6% male). Nearly three quarters (72.6%) of patients reported never feeling self-stigma. HBQOL scores improved across all six domains ( p < 0.001 for each), with the largest relative gains in psychological well-being (60% reduction), transmission concerns (55%), and stigma (53%). Conclusions: HBsAg loss was associated with significant improvements in patient-reported stigma and QOL. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating PROMs into hepatitis B virus clinical care to better capture treatment experiences.
abstract_zh: 摘要背景:慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 会带来不良的健康结果,但也可能导致心理社会和生活质量 (QOL) 挑战。乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 丧失,无论是自发的还是由于治疗(即功能性治愈)导致的,都与临床结果的改善相关,但 HBsAg 清除率对患者报告的结果测量 (PROM) 的影响知之甚少。方法:对有慢性乙型肝炎病史且有来自加拿大六个肝病诊所的 HBsAg 清除记录的成年人进行两项调查(乙型肝炎自我污名和乙型肝炎相关生活质量 [HBQOL])。结果:共有 84 名参与者入组(中位年龄:60 岁;53.6% 为男性)。近四分之三(72.6%)的患者表示从未感到自我耻辱。所有六个领域的 HBQOL 分数均有所改善(每个领域 p < 0.001),其中心理健康(减少 60%)、传播担忧(55%)和耻辱(53%)方面的相对收益最大。结论:HBsAg 消失与患者报告的耻辱感和生活质量的显着改善相关。这些发现强调了将 PROM 纳入乙型肝炎病毒临床护理以更好地获取治疗经验的重要性。

title: Hepatitis B Vaccination in People Living with HIV: Bridging the Immunological Gap
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major driver of liver-related morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV (PLWH), yet vaccine-induced protection is frequently suboptimal. HIV-associated immune dysfunction, including CD4+ T-cell depletion, altered antigen presentation, impaired T follicular helper cell support, and B-cell dysregulation, reduces seroprotection after standard recombinant HBV vaccines and may limit durability of antibody responses. Vaccine response is further influenced by HIV viral suppression, age, comorbidities, prior vaccine history, and baseline HBV serologic status, including isolated hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) and occult HBV infection (OBI) considerations. Although antiretroviral therapy (ART) improves vaccine responsiveness, many PLWH fail to achieve protective hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) titers (≥10 mIU/mL) after conventional schedules, or experience antibody waning over time. Current guidelines recommend HBV vaccination for all susceptible PLWH with post-vaccination serologic testing and revaccination for nonresponders. Persistent implementation barriers, including incomplete series, vaccine hesitancy, stigma, and logistical constraints, continue to limit real-world impact. Emerging clinical trial data support CpG-adjuvanted HBV vaccines (HepB-CpG/Heplisav-B) and intensified dosing and schedules (double-dose or four-dose regimens) to improve seroprotection and generate higher peak anti-HBs titers, which may enhance durability. This review synthesizes guideline recommendations, immunologic mechanisms of hyporesponsiveness, predictors of vaccine response, and practical strategies to optimize HBV vaccination in PLWH.

title: Structural barriers drive the intention-action gap in hepatitis B prevention among migrants in Shandong Province, China: a triangulated study of serological, spatial, and behavioral data
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health challenge in China. Migrant workers constitute a highly vulnerable population due to high geographic mobility and occupational vulnerability. Despite public health education efforts, a notable intention-action gap disrupts the HBV care cascade. This study integrates serological, spatial, and behavioral data to investigate whether this gap is primarily driven by cognitive deficits or interrupted by underlying structural barriers. METHODS: A triangulated cross-sectional study was conducted in Yantai, China, involving structured questionnaire surveys (N = 1,184) and serological testing (N = 2,364). The spatial distribution of regional anti-HBs positive rates was mapped using Geographic Information Systems (GIS). An adapted Health Belief Model was tested using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with a Robust Maximum Likelihood estimator to evaluate the disruptive effects of objective structural constraints-specifically, time poverty, economic constraints, and systemic lack of medical insurance. RESULTS: The serologically confirmed anti-HBs positive rate was 51.10% (1,208/2,364), substantially lower than the 70% threshold recommended by the World Health Organization. Spatial analysis revealed significant geographic heterogeneity (χ2 = 74.38, P < 0.001), with higher immunity concentrated in large-scale industrial belts (67.33%) and lower immunity clustered in dispersed service-sector districts (36.81%). SEM results indicated that while external cues strongly predicted HBV knowledge (β = 0.894), knowledge had only a marginal effect on preventive intention (β = 0.192). Preventive intention significantly predicted actual behavior (β = 0.655). However, this motivational process was severely undermined by structural barriers, predominantly time poverty (β = -0.563, P < 0.001), followed by economic constraints (β = -0.278, P < 0.001) and lack of medical insurance (β = -0.056, P = 0.030). CONCLUSIONS: The intention-action gap in HBV prevention among migrant workers is primarily driven by socioeconomic structural barriers-most notably time poverty-while basic HBV knowledge remains a foundational but insufficient condition for preventive action. Achieving the goal of viral hepatitis elimination requires a shift from individual cognitive persuasion to structural interventions, emphasizing workplace-based service delivery, spatially targeted resource allocation, and insurance reforms to alleviate out-of-pocket and opportunity costs.

title_zh: 结构性障碍导致中国山东省流动人口乙型肝炎预防的意向与行动差距:血清学、空间和行为数据的三角研究
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health challenge in China. Migrant workers constitute a highly vulnerable population due to high geographic mobility and occupational vulnerability. Despite public health education efforts, a notable intention-action gap disrupts the HBV care cascade. This study integrates serological, spatial, and behavioral data to investigate whether this gap is primarily driven by cognitive deficits or interrupted by underlying structural barriers. METHODS: A triangulated cross-sectional study was conducted in Yantai, China, involving structured questionnaire surveys (N = 1,184) and serological testing (N = 2,364). The spatial distribution of regional anti-HBs positive rates was mapped using Geographic Information Systems (GIS). An adapted Health Belief Model was tested using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with a Robust Maximum Likelihood estimator to evaluate the disruptive effects of objective structural constraints-specifically, time poverty, economic constraints, and systemic lack of medical insurance. RESULTS: The serologically confirmed anti-HBs positive rate was 51.10% (1,208/2,364), substantially lower than the 70% threshold recommended by the World Health Organization. Spatial analysis revealed significant geographic heterogeneity (χ2 = 74.38, P < 0.001), with higher immunity concentrated in large-scale industrial belts (67.33%) and lower immunity clustered in dispersed service-sector districts (36.81%). SEM results indicated that while external cues strongly predicted HBV knowledge (β = 0.894), knowledge had only a marginal effect on preventive intention (β = 0.192). Preventive intention significantly predicted actual behavior (β = 0.655). However, this motivational process was severely undermined by structural barriers, predominantly time poverty (β = -0.563, P < 0.001), followed by economic constraints (β = -0.278, P < 0.001) and lack of medical insurance (β = -0.056, P = 0.030). CONCLUSIONS: The intention-action gap in HBV prevention among migrant workers is primarily driven by socioeconomic structural barriers-most notably time poverty-while basic HBV knowledge remains a foundational but insufficient condition for preventive action. Achieving the goal of viral hepatitis elimination requires a shift from individual cognitive persuasion to structural interventions, emphasizing workplace-based service delivery, spatially targeted resource allocation, and insurance reforms to alleviate out-of-pocket and opportunity costs.

title: Evaluating the impact of the Hepatitis B Foundation's international storytelling program on empowerment, advocacy, and stigma reduction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B remains a major global public health challenge, characterized by low awareness, underdiagnosis, limited access to care, and persistent stigma. Storytelling has emerged as a promising health communication strategy to humanize disease experiences, reduce stigma, and promote advocacy. This study evaluates the Hepatitis B Foundation's International Storytelling Program and its impact on storytellers' empowerment, confidence, stigma experiences, and advocacy engagement. METHODS: A mixed-methods evaluation was conducted among adults who recorded personal hepatitis B stories through the program. Quantitative data were collected via an immediate post-recording survey (n = 25) and a follow-up survey 3-6 months later (n = 11), assessing satisfaction, emotional responses, confidence, stigma experiences, and advocacy activities. Survey instruments were developed by the study team and were not previously validated, which may limit measurement reliability and comparability across studies. Descriptive statistics were calculated. Fifteen participants were interviewed qualitatively; these individuals were part of an eligible pool of storytellers spanning 22 countries. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using qualitative content analysis with double coding to support coding consistency. Quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated to provide a comprehensive understanding of program impacts. RESULTS: Participants reported high satisfaction and immediate personal benefits, including increased confidence (92%) and perceived preparedness to advocate (96%). At follow-up, participants reported increased comfort discussing hepatitis B (73%) and personal growth (73%), although findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the small sample size. Qualitative findings suggest that storytelling supported emotional processing, identity reframing, and increased willingness to disclose, while also contributing to perceived community awareness and engagement. CONCLUSIONS: The International Storytelling Program is a practical, promising approach for empowering individuals affected by hepatitis B and promoting advocacy and stigma reduction globally. However, results should be interpreted cautiously due to sample size and potential selection bias. Storytelling may serve as a complementary strategy to traditional public health approaches. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

title_zh: 评估乙型肝炎基金会的国际讲故事计划对赋权、宣传和减少耻辱的影响。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B remains a major global public health challenge, characterized by low awareness, underdiagnosis, limited access to care, and persistent stigma. Storytelling has emerged as a promising health communication strategy to humanize disease experiences, reduce stigma, and promote advocacy. This study evaluates the Hepatitis B Foundation's International Storytelling Program and its impact on storytellers' empowerment, confidence, stigma experiences, and advocacy engagement. METHODS: A mixed-methods evaluation was conducted among adults who recorded personal hepatitis B stories through the program. Quantitative data were collected via an immediate post-recording survey (n = 25) and a follow-up survey 3-6 months later (n = 11), assessing satisfaction, emotional responses, confidence, stigma experiences, and advocacy activities. Survey instruments were developed by the study team and were not previously validated, which may limit measurement reliability and comparability across studies. Descriptive statistics were calculated. Fifteen participants were interviewed qualitatively; these individuals were part of an eligible pool of storytellers spanning 22 countries. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using qualitative content analysis with double coding to support coding consistency. Quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated to provide a comprehensive understanding of program impacts. RESULTS: Participants reported high satisfaction and immediate personal benefits, including increased confidence (92%) and perceived preparedness to advocate (96%). At follow-up, participants reported increased comfort discussing hepatitis B (73%) and personal growth (73%), although findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the small sample size. Qualitative findings suggest that storytelling supported emotional processing, identity reframing, and increased willingness to disclose, while also contributing to perceived community awareness and engagement. CONCLUSIONS: The International Storytelling Program is a practical, promising approach for empowering individuals affected by hepatitis B and promoting advocacy and stigma reduction globally. However, results should be interpreted cautiously due to sample size and potential selection bias. Storytelling may serve as a complementary strategy to traditional public health approaches. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.
abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎仍然是全球主要的公共卫生挑战,其特点是认识低、诊断不足、获得护理的机会有限和持续存在耻辱。讲故事已成为一种很有前途的健康传播策略,可以使疾病体验人性化、减少耻辱并促进宣传。本研究评估了乙型肝炎基金会的国际讲故事计划及其对讲故事者的赋权、信心、耻辱经历和倡导参与的影响。方法:对通过该计划记录个人乙型肝炎故事的成年人进行了混合方法评估。通过立即进行录音后调查 (n = 25) 和 3-6 个月后的跟踪调查 (n = 11) 收集定量数据,评估满意度、情绪反应、信心、耻辱经历和宣传活动。调查工具是由研究团队开发的,之前未经验证,这可能会限制研究之间的测量可靠性和可比性。计算描述性统计数据。十五名参与者接受了定性访谈;这些人属于跨越 22 个国家的合格讲故事者群体的一部分。使用定性内容分析和双重编码来转录和分析访谈,以支持编码一致性。定量和定性研究结果相结合,以提供对计划影响的全面了解。结果:参与者报告了高满意度和直接的个人利益,包括信心增强 (92%) 和感知的倡导准备度 (96%)。在随访中,参与者报告说,讨论乙型肝炎 (73%) 和个人成长 (73%) 的舒适度有所提高,但由于样本量较小,应谨慎解释研究结果。定性研究结果表明,讲故事支持情感处理、身份重构和增加披露意愿,同时也有助于提高社区意识和参与度。结论:国际讲故事计划是一种实用且有前途的方法,可以增强乙型肝炎患者的权能,并在全球范围内促进宣传和减少耻辱。然而,由于样本量和潜在的选择偏差,应谨慎解释结果。讲故事可以作为传统公共卫生方法的补充策略。试用注册:不适用。

title: Longitudinal Patterns of Chronic Hepatitis B Care and Treatment Adherence in Australia: A National Linked Data Cohort Study.
abstract: Current uptake of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) treatment and care in Australia is well below target levels, leading to an ongoing burden of preventable liver disease and cancer. Understanding individual-level trajectories of care engagement and variation by sociodemographic factors is essential to guide efforts to improve access to and retention in care. This study analysed records of hepatitis B viral load (VL) testing and antiviral treatment provided through Australia's national health insurance system, which were linked to migration, death, and sociodemographic data from various government datasets. Treatment and VL testing by population group were assessed, and uptake was calculated using modelled estimates of the number living with CHB. VL testing frequency and treatment adherence based on scripts dispensed were also assessed. Of the estimated 219,800 people living with CHB in Australia in 2023, 118,334 (53.8%) received either VL testing or treatment during 2014-2023. Estimated uptake of VL testing and treatment uptake were lower among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and also varied by region of birth. Of the 81,360 who received any VL testing, only 17,352 (21.3%) received it regularly, while 31,715 (39.0%) had evidence of prior monitoring but no VL testing since 2019. The majority of those who initiated treatment continued therapy and received supply sufficient for adherence. This study shows that substantial gaps exist in CHB care in Australia, particularly in continued monitoring among those not on treatment. Disparities in uptake are evident by priority population. Re-engaging those lost to follow-up should be prioritised.

title_zh: 澳大利亚慢性乙型肝炎护理和治疗依从性的纵向模式:国家关联数据队列研究。
source_body_en: Current uptake of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) treatment and care in Australia is well below target levels, leading to an ongoing burden of preventable liver disease and cancer. Understanding individual-level trajectories of care engagement and variation by sociodemographic factors is essential to guide efforts to improve access to and retention in care. This study analysed records of hepatitis B viral load (VL) testing and antiviral treatment provided through Australia's national health insurance system, which were linked to migration, death, and sociodemographic data from various government datasets. Treatment and VL testing by population group were assessed, and uptake was calculated using modelled estimates of the number living with CHB. VL testing frequency and treatment adherence based on scripts dispensed were also assessed. Of the estimated 219,800 people living with CHB in Australia in 2023, 118,334 (53.8%) received either VL testing or treatment during 2014-2023. Estimated uptake of VL testing and treatment uptake were lower among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and also varied by region of birth. Of the 81,360 who received any VL testing, only 17,352 (21.3%) received it regularly, while 31,715 (39.0%) had evidence of prior monitoring but no VL testing since 2019. The majority of those who initiated treatment continued therapy and received supply sufficient for adherence. This study shows that substantial gaps exist in CHB care in Australia, particularly in continued monitoring among those not on treatment. Disparities in uptake are evident by priority population. Re-engaging those lost to follow-up should be prioritised.

title: Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk Between Untreated Immune Tolerant Vs. Treated Immune Active Chronic Hepatitis B Patients.
abstract: The risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) between chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients in the untreated immune tolerant (U-IT) vs. treated immune active (T-IA) phases is not clear, and most data are in Asian populations. We aim to evaluate long-term risks of cirrhosis, HCC, and overall mortality between U-IT vs. T-IA CHB patients among a national cohort of U.S. We conducted a propensity score weighted analysis of Veterans with CHB who met criteria for U-IT or T-IA from 1/1/2010 to 12/31/2021 (with follow-up through 12/31/2024). Incidence of cirrhosis, HCC, or death were compared between U-IT and T-IA groups. A total of 591 U-IT and 555 T-IA CHB patients were identified (mean age 56.4-57.5 years, 45%-50% non-Hispanic white, 37%-40% African American, 9%-10% Asian, 25%-29% concurrent diabetes, 35%-39% with FIB-4 > 3.25). Over a median follow up of 6.4 years (IQR 3.0-10.4), incidence of HCC was significantly lower in U-IT patients vs. T-IA patients (0.28 vs. 0.54 per 100 person-years; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.32-0.83, p = 0.007). However, the risk of cirrhosis or all-cause mortality was similar between both T-IA and U-IT CHB patients. Among a predominantly non-Asian cohort of adults with CHB, we observed that HCC risk was lower in U-IT patients compared to T-IA patients. While this contrasts with some studies in Asian countries, these data do emphasize the importance of prioritizing and ensuring timely therapy for CHB patients in the IA phase. However, routine treatment in IT patients remains controversial and more data are needed to better understand long-term outcomes.

title_zh: 未经治疗的免疫耐受者与免疫耐受者之间的肝细胞癌风险治疗免疫活跃的慢性乙型肝炎患者。
source_body_en: The risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) between chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients in the untreated immune tolerant (U-IT) vs. treated immune active (T-IA) phases is not clear, and most data are in Asian populations. We aim to evaluate long-term risks of cirrhosis, HCC, and overall mortality between U-IT vs. T-IA CHB patients among a national cohort of U.S. We conducted a propensity score weighted analysis of Veterans with CHB who met criteria for U-IT or T-IA from 1/1/2010 to 12/31/2021 (with follow-up through 12/31/2024). Incidence of cirrhosis, HCC, or death were compared between U-IT and T-IA groups. A total of 591 U-IT and 555 T-IA CHB patients were identified (mean age 56.4-57.5 years, 45%-50% non-Hispanic white, 37%-40% African American, 9%-10% Asian, 25%-29% concurrent diabetes, 35%-39% with FIB-4 > 3.25). Over a median follow up of 6.4 years (IQR 3.0-10.4), incidence of HCC was significantly lower in U-IT patients vs. T-IA patients (0.28 vs. 0.54 per 100 person-years; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.32-0.83, p = 0.007). However, the risk of cirrhosis or all-cause mortality was similar between both T-IA and U-IT CHB patients. Among a predominantly non-Asian cohort of adults with CHB, we observed that HCC risk was lower in U-IT patients compared to T-IA patients. While this contrasts with some studies in Asian countries, these data do emphasize the importance of prioritizing and ensuring timely therapy for CHB patients in the IA phase. However, routine treatment in IT patients remains controversial and more data are needed to better understand long-term outcomes.

title: Predictors of Incident High-Risk Varices in Patients with Hepatitis B-related Cirrhosis Receiving Nucleos(t)ide Analogue Therapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB)-related cirrhosis, routine endoscopic surveillance may be deferred in the absence of high-risk varices (HRV). We aimed to identify predictors of incident HRV in this population. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with CHB-related cirrhosis who initiated NA therapy between March 2008 and June 2020 and were followed through May 2024. Eligible patients underwent baseline and on-treatment upper endoscopy. Patients with baseline HRV, prior variceal ligation, use of nonselective beta-blockers, other viral hepatitis, alcohol overuse, or malignancy were excluded. The cumulative incidence of HRV and adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios (aSHRs) were estimated using competing-risk methods. A point-based risk prediction model was derived from multivariable regression coefficients. RESULTS: Among the 110 included patients, 14 (12.7%) developed HRV over a median follow-up of 3.6 years (IQR, 2.0-5.6). In multivariable analysis, FIB-4 ≥4.0 (aSHR 9.77; 95% CI, 1.45-65.7), coexisting metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) (aSHR 6.37; 95% CI, 1.84-22.0), and albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) grade >1 (aSHR 3.02; 95% CI, 1.21-7.55) were independently associated with incident HRV and were assigned 3, 2 and 1 point, respectively, in the prediction model. At 3 years, the cumulative incidence of HRV was 1.5% (95% CI, 0-4.5) in the low-risk group (0-3 points) and 21.4% (95% CI, 8.0-34.8) in the high-risk group (4-6 points) (P=0.001). CONCLUSION: MASLD, FIB-4 and ALBI grade predict incident HRV in NA-treated CHB cirrhosis, enabling risk-stratified endoscopic surveillance.

title_zh: 接受核苷(酸)类似物治疗的乙型肝炎相关肝硬化患者发生高风险静脉曲张的预测因素。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: In patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB)-related cirrhosis, routine endoscopic surveillance may be deferred in the absence of high-risk varices (HRV). We aimed to identify predictors of incident HRV in this population. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with CHB-related cirrhosis who initiated NA therapy between March 2008 and June 2020 and were followed through May 2024. Eligible patients underwent baseline and on-treatment upper endoscopy. Patients with baseline HRV, prior variceal ligation, use of nonselective beta-blockers, other viral hepatitis, alcohol overuse, or malignancy were excluded. The cumulative incidence of HRV and adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios (aSHRs) were estimated using competing-risk methods. A point-based risk prediction model was derived from multivariable regression coefficients. RESULTS: Among the 110 included patients, 14 (12.7%) developed HRV over a median follow-up of 3.6 years (IQR, 2.0-5.6). In multivariable analysis, FIB-4 ≥4.0 (aSHR 9.77; 95% CI, 1.45-65.7), coexisting metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) (aSHR 6.37; 95% CI, 1.84-22.0), and albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) grade >1 (aSHR 3.02; 95% CI, 1.21-7.55) were independently associated with incident HRV and were assigned 3, 2 and 1 point, respectively, in the prediction model. At 3 years, the cumulative incidence of HRV was 1.5% (95% CI, 0-4.5) in the low-risk group (0-3 points) and 21.4% (95% CI, 8.0-34.8) in the high-risk group (4-6 points) (P=0.001). CONCLUSION: MASLD, FIB-4 and ALBI grade predict incident HRV in NA-treated CHB cirrhosis, enabling risk-stratified endoscopic surveillance.

title: Medication adherence in Chinese adults with chronic hepatitis B based on theory of planned behavior
abstract: Purpose To investigate the factors related to medication adherence in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection by considering the theory of planned behavior (TPB). Methods In this cross-sectional study, medication adherence information was collected from outpatients with CHB in China. Pearson correlation analysis was performed to evaluate the association between medication adherence and TPB items. A structural equation model was established to further assess the effects of the latent TPB variables on medication adherence. Results A total of 225 patients with CHB recruited from the outpatient department of Qingdao Public Health Clinical Center were included, 67.6% of whom reported moderate medication adherence, as assessed using Morisky Adherence Assessment Score. Medication adherence was significantly positively correlated with behavioral intention ( r = 0.51, P < 0.001), perceived behavioral control ( r = 0.63, P < 0.001), and subjective norms ( r = 0.52, P < 0.001). Perceived behavioral control both directly and indirectly affected medication adherence, with the correlation coefficients being 0.14 and 0.32, respectively. The structural equation model revealed behavioral attitude and subjective norms as the strongest predictors of medication adherence, both of which indirectly affected behavior (correlation coefficients: 0.13 × 0.66 = 0.09 and 0.39 × 0.66 = 0.25, respectively). The optimal fitted model of TPB variables explained 58.5% of the variance in medication adherence. Conclusions Moderate medication adherence was discovered among Chinese adults with CHB. Behavioral attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control indirectly affected medication adherence.

title: HBcAg-Induced IL-17F drives liver fibrosis in occult HBV infection
abstract: ABSTRACT While occult hepatitis B virus infection is a known risk factor for progressive liver diseases, the mechanistic basis for this association is poorly understood. To investigate this, we conducted a comparative study involving 40 OBI blood donors and 100 healthy blood donors to assess clinical parameters of liver fibrosis, including serum biomarkers, the FIB-4 index, and liver stiffness measurement. Transcriptome sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from these donors identified IL-17F as significantly upregulated in the OBI group. Mechanistically, we found that IL-17F was chiefly secreted by CD4 + T cells upon HBcAg stimulation and functionally promoted the expression of key fibrosis-related cytokines and markers. Collectively, our study unveils a novel pathway wherein HBcAg induces CD4 + T cells to secrete IL-17F, which in turn accelerates liver fibrogenesis, providing a mechanistic basis for OBI-associated liver disease. IMPORTANCE This study reveals, for the first time, a novel mechanism by which OBI drives liver fibrosis, demonstrating that HBcAg stimulates CD4 + T cells to secrete IL-17F, which in turn activates macrophages and hepatic stellate cells, thereby promoting liver inflammation and fibrosis. This discovery not only elucidates a key molecular pathway underlying OBI-related liver disease progression, but also provides an important theoretical foundation for developing IL-17F-targeted diagnostic approaches and anti-fibrotic therapies.

source_records.abstract: ABSTRACT While occult hepatitis B virus infection is a known risk factor for progressive liver diseases, the mechanistic basis for this association is poorly understood. To investigate this, we conducted a comparative study involving 40 OBI blood donors and 100 healthy blood donors to assess clinical parameters of liver fibrosis, including serum biomarkers, the FIB-4 index, and liver stiffness measurement. Transcriptome sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from these donors identified IL-17F as significantly upregulated in the OBI group. Mechanistically, we found that IL-17F was chiefly secreted by CD4 + T cells upon HBcAg stimulation and functionally promoted the expression of key fibrosis-related cytokines and markers. Collectively, our study unveils a novel pathway wherein HBcAg induces CD4 + T cells to secrete IL-17F, which in turn accelerates liver fibrogenesis, providing a mechanistic basis for OBI-associated liver disease. IMPORTANCE This study reveals, for the first time, a novel mechanism by which OBI drives liver fibrosis, demonstrating that HBcAg stimulates CD4 + T cells to secrete IL-17F, which in turn activates macrophages and hepatic stellate cells, thereby promoting liver inflammation and fibrosis. This discovery not only elucidates a key molecular pathway underlying OBI-related liver disease progression, but also provides an important theoretical foundation for developing IL-17F-targeted diagnostic approaches and anti-fibrotic therapies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Occult hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with progressive liver diseases, but the mechanistic basis remains unclear. The study aimed to elucidate how occult HBV infection contributes to liver fibrosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A comparative study was conducted involving 40 occult HBV infection (OBI) blood donors and 100 healthy blood donors to evaluate liver fibrosis parameters. The study assessed clinical markers including serum biomarkers, the FIB-4 index, and liver stiffness measurement.
analysis.methods: Transcriptome sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells identified IL-17F as upregulated in the OBI group. Mechanistic experiments demonstrated that IL-17F was primarily secreted by CD4+ T cells upon HBcAg stimulation and promoted fibrosis-related cytokine and marker expression.
analysis.main_results: IL-17F was chiefly secreted by CD4+ T cells following HBcAg stimulation and functionally enhanced the expression of fibrosis-related cytokines and markers.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study reveals a novel pathway in which HBcAg induces CD4+ T cells to secrete IL-17F, which accelerates liver fibrogenesis, providing a mechanistic basis for OBI-associated liver disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest potential targets for IL-17F-based diagnostic approaches and anti-fibrotic therapies in OBI-related liver disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to the abstract and lacks detailed methodological, statistical, or validation data, warranting cautious interpretation of the mechanistic pathway and its clinical implications.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the mechanistic basis of liver fibrosis in occult HBV infection (OBI) by comparing 40 OBI blood donors with 100 healthy controls. Transcriptome sequencing identified IL-17F as upregulated in OBI donors, and mechanistic experiments showed that IL-17F was secreted by CD4+ T cells upon HBcAg stimulation, promoting fibrosis-related cytokine expression. The authors propose a novel pathway where HBcAg drives IL-17F-mediated liver fibrogenesis, offering a potential mechanistic explanation for OBI-associated liver disease. The findings suggest IL-17F as a target for diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, though the evidence is confined to the abstract and lacks detailed validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 隐匿性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染与进行性肝病相关,但其机制尚不清楚。该研究旨在阐明隐匿性乙型肝炎病毒感染如何导致肝纤维化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 40 名隐匿性 HBV 感染 (OBI) 献血者和 100 名健康献血者进行了一项比较研究,以评估肝纤维化参数。该研究评估了临床标志物,包括血清生物标志物、FIB-4 指数和肝脏硬度测量。
elements_zh.methods: 外周血单核细胞的转录组测序发现 OBI 组中 IL-17F 表达上调。机制实验表明,IL-17F 主要由 CD4+ T 细胞在 HBcAg 刺激后分泌,并促进纤维化相关细胞因子和标志物的表达。
elements_zh.main_results: IL-17F 主要由 HBcAg 刺激后的 CD4+ T 细胞分泌,并在功能上增强纤维化相关细胞因子和标志物的表达。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究揭示了 HBcAg 诱导 CD4+ T 细胞分泌 IL-17F 的新途径,从而加速肝纤维化,为 OBI 相关肝病提供了机制基础。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,基于 IL-17F 的诊断方法和抗纤维化治疗 OBI 相关肝病的潜在靶点。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于摘要,缺乏详细的方法学、统计或验证数据,需要对机制途径及其临床意义进行谨慎解释。

title: Chronic HBV Infection Disrupts CCL5‐Secreting cNK Cells and Attenuates Liver Accumulation and Activation of DCs and HBV‐Specific T Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the immunological mechanisms underlying chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection‐induced immune tolerance is critical for developing effective therapeutic strategies, yet the mechanisms by which natural killer (NK)‐cell subsets regulate dendritic cell (DC)‐mediated antiviral immunity during chronic HBV infection remain unclear. Here, we demonstrated that chronic HBV infection disrupted intrahepatic DCs accumulation and activation by suppressing CC chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5) production from hepatic NK cells. Importantly, chronic HBV infection reduced the number of hepatic conventional NK (cNK) cells, the main source of hepatic CCL5, whereas liver‐resident NK (LrNK) cells increased and exhibited lower CCL5 expression and immunosuppressive features. Adoptive transfer of CCL5‐competent hepatic cNK cells promoted DCs accumulation and activation, enhanced HBV‐specific CD8 + T‐cell responses, and facilitated viral clearance. Mechanistically, chronic HBV infection promoted the activation of adenosine A2a receptor (ADORA2A)/nuclear factor kappa‐B (NF‐κB) pathway in hepatic NK cells, thereby antagonizing NF‐κB activation, reducing the proportion of cNK cells, suppressing CCL5 production, and ultimately impairing hepatic aggregation and activation of DCs, leading to defective anti‐HBV immune responses. This study revealed a novel mechanism involved in chronic HBV infection‐induced immune tolerance and indicated that targeting the ADORA2A/NFκB/CCL5 axis in cNK cells may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for chronic HBV infection.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 摘要:了解慢性乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染引起的免疫耐受的免疫机制对于制定有效的治疗策略至关重要,但自然杀伤 (NK) 细胞亚群在慢性 HBV 感染期间调节树突状细胞 (DC) 介导的抗病毒免疫的机制仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究揭示了慢性 HBV 感染诱导的免疫耐受的新机制,并表明靶向 cNK 细胞中的 ADORA2A/NFκB/CCL5 轴可能代表慢性 HBV 感染的潜在治疗策略。
elements_zh.methods: 所提供的证据没有明确说明核心实验、分析或统计方法。
elements_zh.main_results: 重要的是,慢性 HBV 感染减少了肝脏常规 NK (cNK) 细胞(肝脏 CCL5 的主要来源)的数量,而肝脏驻留 NK (LrNK) 细胞增加并表现出较低的 CCL5 表达和免疫抑制特征。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这里,我们证明慢性 HBV 感染通过抑制肝 NK 细胞产生 CC 趋化因子配体 5 (CCL5) 来破坏肝内 DC 的积累和激活。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 从机制上讲,慢性HBV感染促进肝NK细胞中腺苷A2a受体(ADORA2A)/核因子κB(NF-κB)通路的激活,从而拮抗NF-κB激活,降低cNK细胞比例,抑制CCL5产生,最终损害肝脏聚集和DCs激活,导致抗HBV免疫反应缺陷。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: CCL5 活性肝 cNK 细胞的过继转移促进了 DC 的积累和激活,增强了 HBV 特异性 CD8 + T 细胞反应,并促进了病毒清除。

title: NGS-diagnosed HBV encephalitis with isolated left parietal lobe involvement: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Viral encephalitis refers to the inflammation of the brain parenchyma caused by viral infection, usually manifested as fever, unconsciousness, seizures, and meningeal irritation symptoms. The non-specific clinical manifestations, combined with incomplete medical history, often lead to missed diagnoses and inappropriate treatments. Case presentation We present a case of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) encephalitis, manifesting as isolated left parietal lobe involvement. The patient is a chronic hepatitis B virus carrier who did not receive antiviral therapy. Upon onset, the main symptoms were unconsciousness, fever, and seizures. He was diagnosed with HBV encephalitis thru next-generation sequencing (NGS) testing of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). After antiviral treatment with entecavir and general symptomatic treatment, the patient’s clinical symptoms disappeared, and a follow-up brain MRI showed that the lesion had almost completely resolved. Conclusions Central nervous system (CNS) infections caused by HBV are incredibly uncommon in clinical practice. This case highlights that the clinical manifestations of HBV encephalitis are nonspecific and prone to being missed, while neuroimaging often reveals an isolated lesion. Early application of NGS for accurate pathogen diagnosis is crucial to reduce misdiagnosis.

source_records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Viral encephalitis refers to the inflammation of the brain parenchyma caused by viral infection, usually manifested as fever, unconsciousness, seizures, and meningeal irritation symptoms. The non-specific clinical manifestations, combined with incomplete medical history, often lead to missed diagnoses and inappropriate treatments. CASE PRESENTATION: We present a case of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) encephalitis, manifesting as isolated left parietal lobe involvement. The patient is a chronic hepatitis B virus carrier who did not receive antiviral therapy. Upon onset, the main symptoms were unconsciousness, fever, and seizures. He was diagnosed with HBV encephalitis thru next-generation sequencing (NGS) testing of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). After antiviral treatment with entecavir and general symptomatic treatment, the patient's clinical symptoms disappeared, and a follow-up brain MRI showed that the lesion had almost completely resolved. CONCLUSIONS: Central nervous system (CNS) infections caused by HBV are incredibly uncommon in clinical practice. This case highlights that the clinical manifestations of HBV encephalitis are nonspecific and prone to being missed, while neuroimaging often reveals an isolated lesion. Early application of NGS for accurate pathogen diagnosis is crucial to reduce misdiagnosis.

title: Outcomes of nucleos(t)ide analogue discontinuation following finite xalnesiran-based therapies in chronic hepatitis B.
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Novel regimens aimed at achieving functional cure of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in virologically suppressed participants require the withdrawal of nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA). However, data from clinical trials are limited. METHODS: Piranga is a Phase 2 platform trial that evaluated 4 xalnesiran regimens with or without an immunomodulator in virologically suppressed participants with CHB. All participants continued the established NA therapy until NA stopping criteria were met at the end of treatment or during follow-up. Participants who stopped NA were monitored and restarted NA if restarting criteria were met. This post hoc evaluation reports the NA discontinuation events and outcomes. RESULTS: Among 121 participants, 58 (48%) met NA stopping criteria and 40 (33%) discontinued NA. Of these 40, 17 (43%) met NA restarting criteria, 16 (40%) restarted NA, and 24 (60%) remained off NA by the end of the study (EOS). Among participants who remained off NA, 5 achieved and maintained HBsAg loss (HBsAg <0.05 IU/mL) and HBV DNA undetectable (HBV DNA <10 IU/mL); all were in treatment arms with an immunomodulator. Of the 40 participants who discontinued NA, 19 (48%) experienced virological relapse (VR), 3 (8%) of whom further developed clinical relapse (CR). The majority of participants restarted NA following VR. VR and CR events were associated with preserved liver function and resolved without sequelae. CONCLUSIONS: NA discontinuation after xalnesiran-based therapy was safely managed with the application of prespecified NA stopping and restarting criteria and close monitoring. Five participants achieved and maintained HBsAg loss and undetectable HBV DNA while off NA until EOS. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: NCT04225715.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) requires novel regimens to achieve functional cure, but withdrawal of nucleos(t)ide analogues (NA) poses safety and efficacy challenges due to limited clinical trial data on outcomes after NA discontinuation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Piranga is a Phase 2 platform trial evaluating four xalnesiran regimens with or without an immunomodulator in virologically suppressed CHB participants, where NA was discontinued after predefined stopping criteria were met and restarted if relapse occurred.
analysis.methods: Participants continued NA until stopping criteria were met; those who discontinued NA were monitored and restarted if virological or clinical relapse criteria were triggered, with outcomes tracked until the end of study.
analysis.main_results: Among 121 participants, 40 (33%) discontinued NA; 16 (40%) restarted NA, 24 (60%) remained off NA by study end, 5 achieved sustained HBsAg loss and undetectable HBV DNA off NA, 19 (48%) experienced virological relapse, and 3 (8%) developed clinical relapse.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that NA discontinuation after xalnesiran-based therapy can be safely managed with prespecified criteria and close monitoring, with a subset achieving functional cure markers, highlighting the potential of xalnesiran-based regimens in CHB management.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the feasibility of NA discontinuation in carefully monitored settings and suggest xalnesiran-based therapies may contribute to functional cure in a subset of CHB patients, informing future treatment strategies and trial designs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a Phase 2 platform trial with a post hoc evaluation, lacks randomization or comparator arms, and relies on predefined stopping/restarting criteria, warranting cautious interpretation and larger controlled studies to confirm safety and efficacy.

analysis.summary_en: This Phase 2 platform trial evaluated xalnesiran-based regimens in virologically suppressed chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients, assessing outcomes after nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) discontinuation. Among 121 participants, 40 (33%) discontinued NA, with 24 (60%) remaining off therapy by study end. Five participants achieved sustained HBsAg loss and undetectable HBV DNA off NA, while 19 (48%) experienced virological relapse and 3 (8%) developed clinical relapse. NA discontinuation was managed using prespecified criteria and close monitoring, demonstrating safety without sequelae. The study suggests xalnesiran-based therapies may facilitate functional cure in a subset of patients, though findings are limited by the trial's design and lack of randomization.

title_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎基于 Xalnesiran 的有限疗法后停用核苷(酸)类似物的结果。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Novel regimens aimed at achieving functional cure of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in virologically suppressed participants require the withdrawal of nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA). However, data from clinical trials are limited. METHODS: Piranga is a Phase 2 platform trial that evaluated 4 xalnesiran regimens with or without an immunomodulator in virologically suppressed participants with CHB. All participants continued the established NA therapy until NA stopping criteria were met at the end of treatment or during follow-up. Participants who stopped NA were monitored and restarted NA if restarting criteria were met. This post hoc evaluation reports the NA discontinuation events and outcomes. RESULTS: Among 121 participants, 58 (48%) met NA stopping criteria and 40 (33%) discontinued NA. Of these 40, 17 (43%) met NA restarting criteria, 16 (40%) restarted NA, and 24 (60%) remained off NA by the end of the study (EOS). Among participants who remained off NA, 5 achieved and maintained HBsAg loss (HBsAg <0.05 IU/mL) and HBV DNA undetectable (HBV DNA <10 IU/mL); all were in treatment arms with an immunomodulator. Of the 40 participants who discontinued NA, 19 (48%) experienced virological relapse (VR), 3 (8%) of whom further developed clinical relapse (CR). The majority of participants restarted NA following VR. VR and CR events were associated with preserved liver function and resolved without sequelae. CONCLUSIONS: NA discontinuation after xalnesiran-based therapy was safely managed with the application of prespecified NA stopping and restarting criteria and close monitoring. Five participants achieved and maintained HBsAg loss and undetectable HBV DNA while off NA until EOS. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: NCT04225715.
