full_text: Article summary AI generated Hepatitis B (HBV) and C (HCV) infections pose significant public health challenges in India, particularly in regions like Jammu and Kashmir, where their prevalence is believed to be higher than the national average. This study revealed a seroprevalence of 3.42% for HBV and 18.30% for HCV among patients in North Kashmir, identifying intravenous drug use as a major risk factor for HCV transmission, thereby underscoring the urgent need for targeted screening and intervention strategies in the region. Abstract Background India has a high burden of endemic HBV and HCV infections, with national seroprevalence of 0.95% for HBV and 0.32% for HCV. In Jammu and Kashmir, the prevalence of HBV and HCV is believed to be elevated much higher than the national average. The ever-increasing incidence of both HBV and HCV infections demand region-specific screening to assess the burden of disease, risk factors and plan control measures. Methods A cross- sectional study was conducted at a tertiary-care hospital in North Kashmir, India, from September 2023-November 2024.Enzyme linked immunosorbent assay(ELISA) method was used for screening Hepatitis B surface antigen and antibodies against HCV. The risk factors associated with HBV and HCV infections were analyzed statistically by using logistic regression model. The model was evaluated using AUC-ROC and F1 score. Results A total of 1081 and 1087 samples were analyzed for HBsAg and anti-HCV, which showed prevalence of 3.42% and 18.30%, respectively. Among the identified risk factors, intra venous drug usage (aOR = 18.4, P =0.000) represents the most common means of HCV transmission. Additionally, other risk factors like fever, patient type, age group of 20–40 years, and planned surgery showed statistically significant associations with HCV infection. Conclusion The study highlights the alarming burden of HBV and HCV infection in North Kashmir compared to the national prevalence. The high prevalence of HCV infection and HBV/HCV co-infection particularly among the young population, calls for urgent, region specific screening and early diagnosis to prevent further spread of viral hepatitis infection. Similar content being viewed by others 1 Introduction Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections remain a significant public health issue due to their high prevalence and fatality rates [1]. Most liver illnesses worldwide are caused by infections with the hepatitis B and C viruses (HCV and HBV) [2]. HBV affects approximately one-third of the global population, with an estimated 350–400 million chronically afflicted, and results in one million deaths annually [3]. HBV infections are distributed globally, however, the majority of infected individuals live in Asia, the Middle East, and Africa [4]. In high-endemic regions like Africa and the Western Pacific, the prevalence of the hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) can reach as high as 8.83% and 5.26%, respectively, with a global prevalence of 3.61% [3]. Moreover, the World Health Organization (WHO) has estimated that there are 50 million people having chronic hepatitis C infection, with about 1 million new infections being added every year and approximately, 242,000 people died from hepatitis C, mostly from cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in the year 2022 alone [5, 6]. The frequency and prevalence of HBV and HCV vary noticeably by location; this could be because of poor health facilities, low socioeconomic position, and lack of public awareness about the spread of deadly infectious illnesses [7]. The use of non-sterile equipment during medical procedures, the transfusion of infected blood, any breach in infection control practices and sharing of needles are the routes through which HBV and HCV may propagate. Pregnancy and sexual contact are other routes through which these viruses can spread vertically and horizontally [8]. As per the comprehensive data published by the National Centre for Disease Control, Directorate General of Health Services Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (NCDC, 2021), India has a high burden of endemic HBV and HCV infections, with national seroprevalence of 0.95% for HBV and 0.32% for HCV. While some states, especially in the Southern India (Andhra Pradesh and Telangana) reported a higher seroprevalence of HBV (2.7%) than the national average followed by some northeastern states (Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram etc.). Jammu and Kashmir, along with Himachal Pradesh, were reported to have the lowest seroprevalence of both HBV and HCV infections, with less than 0.5% and 0.02%, respectively. However, recent reports indicate surge in the seroprevalence of HBV and HCV across Jammu and Kashmir [9] primarily due to the exponential increase in the number of people using intravenous drug abuse among other reasons. Thus, the purpose of this study was to ascertain the seroprevalence of HBsAg and anti-HCV antibodies and identify associated risk factors among patients who were visiting Associated Hospital of Government Medical College Baramulla with clinically suspected viral hepatitis. This represents the first hospital-based study on the seroprevalence of HBV and HCV in North Kashmir, Baramulla using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay(ELISA) method, offering novel and regional specific epidemiological insights. 2 Materials and methods This cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Microbiology Government Medical College, Baramulla, from September 2023 to November 2024. The samples were collected by adopting convenience sampling, in which participants were selected based on their accessibility to the hospital services. The selected patients belonged primarily to district Baramulla, however patients from adjoining districts of Kupwara and Bandipora comprising the entire North Kashmir were also analyzed in this study. 2.1 Inclusion criteria The study involved individuals of both sexes and all age groups from inpatient (IP) and outpatient departments (OPD) who were recommended for HBV and HCV screening by their treating clinicians and were willing to get tested. 2.2 Exclusion criteria Patients who were not willing to get tested were excluded from the study. Moreover, the patients with previous positive tests were excluded to prevent duplication and ensure the accuracy of the data analysis. 2.3 Methodology About 5 mL of whole blood was collected aseptically in a plain red top tube (clot activator) and transported in a box maintained at 2–8 °C to serology laboratory. The samples were processed within 24–48 hours. The serum was separated in a sterile 1.5 mL vials and then tested using ELISA. The HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) was assayed using HEPALISA for HBsAg and the HCV antibody was assayed by HCV Microlisa as per the manufacturer’s instructions (J. Mitra & Co. Pvt. Ltd., New Delhi, India). All the samples were accompanied by demographic and geographical details of the patient. Patients were assessed for the presence of risk factors such as past invasive procedures like surgery, dental extraction, intravenous drug abuse or renal dialysis and the findings were noted. Assay runs were strictly performed following standard operating procedures, including quality controls. 2.4 Statistical analysis The data obtained from HBV and HCV testing and risk factor evaluation were statistically analyzed by using R-programming (version 4.4.2). The association between categorical variables and seroprevalence of HBV and HCV was evaluated using Fisher’s exact test and Pearson’s χ2 test. The data obtained is presented and summarized (Tables 1, 2, 3). Moreover, logistic regression analysis was also used to determine the association between independent predictors of HCV seroprevalence, adjusting for sex, age category, and identified risk factors. Finally, adjusted odds ratios (AORs) were computed to evaluate the degree of association between reported risk factors and HCV infection. Moreover, the performance of logistic regression model was done by evaluating accuracy, F1 score, and area under the curve-receiver operating characteristic (ROC-AUC). 3 Results A total of 1081 patients were tested for HBsAg, out of whom 704 (65.12%) were males and 377 (34.87%) were females. 37 out of 1081 patients were found to be positive for the presence of HBsAg showing an overall seroprevalence of 3.42% among the tested individuals. 28 out of 37 positive patients were males and the rest 9 were females. Similarly, 1087 suspected patients were tested for anti-HCV antibodies, out of whom 711 (65.40%) were males and 376 (34.5%) were females. The anti-HCV antibodies were observed in 199 out of 1087 patients, showing an overall seroprevalence of 18.30% among the tested individuals (Figure 2). Among the positive individuals 188 (26.44%) were males and the remaining 11 (2.93%) were females. The data was further analyzed for co-infection with Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C, a total of 13 patients were found to be infected by both Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C viruses. The rate of co-infection was found to be the highest (2.32%) in the age group 18–35 years followed by above 35 years (0.52%) and age group 0–18 years had the least rate of co-infection. In this investigation the clinical determinants such as IV drug users, surgery, jaundice, patient type, sex, and age category showed statistically significant association with the seroprevalence of HCV infection (p < 0.05 in both tests). IV drug users have the highest odds ratio (23.24), indicating a strong association with seroprevalence of HCV. “Planned for Surgery” category is also significantly associated, but with a lower odds ratio (0.0728). However, other clinical factors including fever, renal dialysis, and others (acute diarrheal disease, chills, rashes, severe acute respiratory infection) did not show a statistically significant relationship with seroprevalence of HCV infection (p > 0.05 in both tests). The odds ratios (OR) for these factors are close to 1, suggesting no strong impact on the prevalence of HCV infection (Table 2). The findings of this study indicate that IV drug usage plays a critical role in HCV transmission (Figure 3). Moreover, further investigations are needed into non-significant factors to confirm whether they truly lack association, or the sample size affects their results. Out of 1081 patients, 37 were tested positive for HBV infection, showing a prevalence rate of 3.42%, the performance of Pearson’s χ2 test and Fisher’s exact test are summarized in Table 3. The seroprevalence of HBV was insignificantly higher (χ2: 0.011; P = 0.914) in men (2.31%) compared to women (1.11%), therefore the HBV infection was not significantly associated with the sex. Similarly, the prevalence of HBV infection was also not significantly associated (P > 0.05) with IV drug users, jaundice, renal dialysis, age category, fever, and patient type (Table III). However, Planned for surgery and other categories (including acute diarrheal disease, chills, rashes, severe acute respiratory infection) were found to be significantly associated (P < 0.05) with HBV infections having χ2 value of 8.9139 and 10.691, respectively. Therefore, the finding of this study suggests that “planned for surgery” and “others” categories were the most likely risk factors associated the transmission of HBV infection. 4 Discussion The importance of hepatitis B and hepatitis C viral infections cannot be overemphasized, given the magnitude of the infections they cause. After the publication of factsheet on seroprevalence of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C based on National Family Health Survey-4 in the year 2021, a comprehensive data on the prevalence of hepatitis B and hepatitis C throughout India was made available to the public for the first time by National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), New Delhi. Therefore, we have compared the data generated in this study primarily to the data presented in the factsheet apart from the individual studies conducted throughout India and at the international level. In the present study, the data from September 2023 till November 2024 was analysed for the incidence and prevalence of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C infections in a tertiary care hospital in the North Kashmir. The prevalence of Hepatitis B was found to be 3.42% which is higher compared to the national average of 0.95%, however, we have observed a prevalence of 18.30% for Hepatitis C which is many folds higher compared to the national average of 0.32%. The reason for the increased prevalence of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C in the present study are due to one or more of the following reasons, this is a hospital based study where generally suspected (both symptomatic and high risk) patients were tested and most of individuals in the hepatitis C positive category belong to the high risk factor (intravenous drug abuse) group, wherein patient clustering is quite common and ELISA was used for the testing instead of more commonly used immunochromatographic method. India falls in intermediate zone of prevalence (2 to 5%) category of the WHO, among the South-East Asian countries (WHO fact sheet on Hepatitis B). Varying percentage of hepatitis B prevalence has been reported from the different states of India, ranging from 0.87% to 21.4% among different populations including in the healthy individuals, hemodialysis patients, patients with acute viral hepatitis and others reviewed by Kumar et al. [10]. Shadaker and co-workers reported prevalence of hepatitis B at 1.4% [11]. Similarly, varying percentage of hepatitis B prevalence has been reported from different provinces of Jammu and Kashmir. Studies from the Ladakh have reported a comparative higher percentage of hepatitis B prevalence at 7.86% [12] and 4.2% [13] and from Jammu province prevalence of 2.44% has been reported [14], 0.92% from Doda district [15]. Kadla and co-workers reported prevalence of Hepatitis B at 2.4% from South Kashmir [16]. None of the risk factors studied were found to be significantly associated (P > 0.05) with the prevalence of HBsAg positivity except the “planned for surgery” category which included people planned for any surgical/invasive procedures including any invasive dental procedures. This association indicates that patients under this category were getting tested for screening before any invasive procedures and did not necessarily have any signs or symptoms of viral hepatitis and were purely detected by chance, indicating the prevalence of sub-clinical Hepatitis B infections prevailing in the community. Similarly, in “others” category a myriad of non-specific complaints like acute diarrheal disease, chills, rashes and severe acute respiratory infection were the common complaints mentioned by the patients and have not been directly implicated in the Hepatitis B infections. Together, both these factors indicate that Hepatitis B is prevalent in the community possibly as carriers and the infection is discovered incidentally during screenings. Therefore, widespread screenings outside the hospital settings need to be carried out to further confirm the prevalence, trends and risk factors associated with Hepatitis B infections. Similarly, the prevalence of Hepatitis C infection also varies across the globe and also among the different states of India. The difference in prevalence of Hepatitis C is multifactorial and may vary based on different healthcare practices, cultural practices, socio-economic status and other behavioral issues. Sood and co-workers reported prevalence of Hepatitis C at 3.6% from Punjab [17], Rajani and Jais reported prevalence of 1.5% from Delhi [18] Mukherjee and co-workers reported prevalence of 24.6% from West Bengal and similarly prevalence ranging from 0% to 49% have been reported in different studies across the globe [19]. Multiple logistic regression analysis was applied to determine the association between clinical factors and seroprevalence of HCV infection. The key clinical factors associated with seroprevalence of HCV infection are listed in table II, which also presents their statistics summary and respective coefficients from the logistic regression analysis, including p-values, adjusted odds ratios (AOR), standard errors, and confidence intervals (CI) for the AOR. Notably, the AOR for IV drug users was determined to be (AOR:18.4, 95% CI: 9–39.49.49). This indicates that IV drug users are about 18.41 times more likely to have HCV infection compared to non-IV drug users. This result suggests a strong association between IV drug use and the occurrence of HCV, and it is statistically significant. Similarly, other factors like patient type (outpatient), fever, certain age groups (20–40), sex, and surgery showed statistically significant associations with HCV infection (15–17). However, jaundice, renal dialysis, other factors were statistically insignificant (Table II). Additionally, the logistic regression model has achieved an accuracy of 88.99%, an ROC_AUC value of 87.2%, and an F1 score of 93.41% (Fig. 1). Therefore, in this comprehensive study, we highlighted the transmission modes of HCV infection and related risk factors. These findings emphasize the implementation of public awareness programmes to promote prevention and control of HCV infections (see Figs. 2, 3). In the present study males were found to be more affected by HCV compared to the females, although with no clinical significance, the similar trends have been reported earlier as well [20,21,22]. However, lack of awareness and associated social stigma faced by females in seeking testing and or treatment cannot be ruled out as a reason for low prevalence in women [23] and hence the aspect needs further exploration by conducting community screening focusing on women. Patients of all age groups were studied; it was found that patients in the age group 20–40 years were more predominantly affected (comprising 32.46% of all positives). In Jammu and Kashmir, the prevalence of HBV and HCV is believed to be elevated much higher than the national average. The ever-increasing incidence of both HBV and HCV infections demand region-specific screening to assess the burden of disease, risk factors and plan control measures. Methods A cross- sectional study was conducted at a tertiary-care hospital in North Kashmir, India, from September 2023-November 2024.Enzyme linked immunosorbent assay(ELISA) method was used for screening Hepatitis B surface antigen and antibodies against HCV. The risk factors associated with HBV and HCV infections were analyzed statistically by using logistic regression model. The model was evaluated using AUC-ROC and F1 score. Results A total of 1081 and 1087 samples were analyzed for HBsAg and anti-HCV, which showed prevalence of 3.42% and 18.30%, respectively. Among the identified risk factors, intra venous drug usage (aOR = 18.4, P =0.000) represents the most common means of HCV transmission. Additionally, other risk factors like fever, patient type, age group of 20–40 years, and planned surgery showed statistically significant associations with HCV infection. Conclusion The study highlights the alarming burden of HBV and HCV infection in North Kashmir compared to the national prevalence. The high prevalence of HCV infection and HBV/HCV co-infection particularly among the young population, calls for urgent, region specific screening and early diagnosis to prevent further spread of viral hepatitis infection. Most liver illnesses worldwide are caused by infections with the hepatitis B and C viruses (HCV and HBV) [2]. HBV affects approximately one-third of the global population, with an estimated 350–400 million chronically afflicted, and results in one million deaths annually [3]. HBV infections are distributed globally, however, the majority of infected individuals live in Asia, the Middle East, and Africa [4]. In high-endemic regions like Africa and the Western Pacific, the prevalence of the hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) can reach as high as 8.83% and 5.26%, respectively, with a global prevalence of 3.61% [3]. Moreover, the World Health Organization (WHO) has estimated that there are 50 million people having chronic hepatitis C infection, with about 1 million new infections being added every year and approximately, 242,000 people died from hepatitis C, mostly from cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in the year 2022 alone [5, 6]. The frequency and prevalence of HBV and HCV vary noticeably by location; this could be because of poor health facilities, low socioeconomic position, and lack of public awareness about the spread of deadly infectious illnesses [7]. The use of non-sterile equipment during medical procedures, the transfusion of infected blood, any breach in infection control practices and sharing of needles are the routes through which HBV and HCV may propagate. title: In Silico Studies of the Hepatitis B Virus Polymerase: Efforts to Identify Novel Drug Binding Sites to Inhibit HBV Replication.
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) replicates via reverse transcription, a reaction catalyzed by the HBV polymerase (P) protein. P is a multidomain protein consists of terminal protein, spacer, reverse transcriptase, and ribonuclease H domains. We used a predicted structural model of HBV P and computationally identified potential non-nucleos(t)ide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) sites. Out of the three potential NNRTI sites, we selected Site 3 for virtual high throughput screening of 837,000 virtual compounds. We selected 53 compounds considering their docking scores, ligand uniqueness, stability and rigidity for screening in HBV replication inhibition assay, but all of them failed to suppress the HBV reverse transcription. Molecular dynamic simulations showed that Site 3 binding pocket is not conformationally stable even after binding of the ligand. This study indicates that additional potential NNRTI sites should be explored, and that rigorous molecular dynamic simulations studies should be performed before virtual compound screening.

title: The Impact of HIV Coinfection on Mpox Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: A substantial proportion of mpox cases occur in people coinfected with HIV. However, the extent to which HIV coinfection and HIV-related immune status influence clinical outcomes, including disease severity and coinfections, remains incompletely characterized. We systematically searched PubMed, Cochrane, EMBASE, and Web of Science from database inception to March 2025 for observational studies comparing clinical outcomes between mpox patients with and without HIV coinfection. The random-effects model was prespecified to pool effect sizes. Dichotomous and continuous outcomes were summarized as risk ratios (RRs) and standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals. Post hoc exploratory subgroup analyses were conducted on the basis of economic development level, HIV viral suppression status, and the proportion of participants with advanced HIV disease (AHD). A total of 29 studies involving 15,522 mpox patients were included, of whom 52.43% were coinfected with HIV. In the primary analyses, HIV coinfection was associated with significantly higher hospitalization rates [RR = 1.50, 95% CI (1.17, 1.93)] and mortality [RR = 4.54, 95% CI (2.11, 9.77)]. Mpox patients with HIV coinfection were more frequently coinfected with syphilis, HBV, and HCV and more commonly presented with fever, proctitis, malaise, rectal irritation syndrome, diarrhoea, skin and soft tissue infections, and pneumonia. Pooled blood test results revealed lower levels of albumin, calcium, and haemoglobin, and higher CK-MB levels in the coinfected group. Skin lesions in the perianal region were more common among coinfected patients. HIV coinfection is associated with substantially greater clinical severity, greater risks of hospitalization and death, and greater rates of sexually transmitted coinfections among mpox patients. Exploratory subgroup analyses further suggest that suboptimal HIV suppression may be a clinically relevant determinant of adverse outcomes, and that skin lesion severity may depend substantially on host immune status. All subgroup findings are post hoc and hypothesis generating and are limited by the aggregate nature of the data. Clinicians should consider intensified monitoring and comprehensive supportive care for mpox patients with HIV coinfection, particularly those with suboptimal suppression. Strengthening vaccination and health education in high-risk populations and optimizing strategies for ART initiation remain crucial for mitigating the public health impact of MPXV.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述调查了 HIV 合并感染对 MPOX 患者的影响,特别检查了临床结果,包括疾病严重程度和合并感染。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 通过搜索 PubMed、Cochrane、EMBASE 和 Web of Science,从数据库建立到 2025 年 3 月,进行了系统回顾和荟萃分析。符合条件的研究是比较患有和不患有 HIV 合并感染的 MPOX 患者的临床结果的观察性研究。共纳入 29 项研究,涉及 15,522 名 MPOX 患者,其中 52.43% 合并感染 HIV。随机效应模型预先指定了池效应大小,二分法和连续结果总结为风险比 (RR) 和标准化均差 (SMD),置信区间为 95%。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 所有亚组研究结果都是事后和假设生成的,并受到数据总体性质的限制。HIV 合并感染和 HIV 相关免疫状态对临床结果(包括疾病严重程度和合并感染)的影响程度尚未完全确定。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 临床医生应考虑对 HIV 合并感染的 MPOX 患者,特别是那些抑制效果不佳的患者,加强监测和全面的支持护理。加强高危人群的疫苗接种和健康教育以及优化 ART 启动策略对于减轻 MPXV 的公共卫生影响仍然至关重要。

title_zh: HIV 合并感染对 Mpox 患者的影响:系统评价和荟萃分析。
source_body_en: A substantial proportion of mpox cases occur in people coinfected with HIV. However, the extent to which HIV coinfection and HIV-related immune status influence clinical outcomes, including disease severity and coinfections, remains incompletely characterized. We systematically searched PubMed, Cochrane, EMBASE, and Web of Science from database inception to March 2025 for observational studies comparing clinical outcomes between mpox patients with and without HIV coinfection. The random-effects model was prespecified to pool effect sizes. Dichotomous and continuous outcomes were summarized as risk ratios (RRs) and standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals. Post hoc exploratory subgroup analyses were conducted on the basis of economic development level, HIV viral suppression status, and the proportion of participants with advanced HIV disease (AHD). A total of 29 studies involving 15,522 mpox patients were included, of whom 52.43% were coinfected with HIV. In the primary analyses, HIV coinfection was associated with significantly higher hospitalization rates [RR = 1.50, 95% CI (1.17, 1.93)] and mortality [RR = 4.54, 95% CI (2.11, 9.77)]. Mpox patients with HIV coinfection were more frequently coinfected with syphilis, HBV, and HCV and more commonly presented with fever, proctitis, malaise, rectal irritation syndrome, diarrhoea, skin and soft tissue infections, and pneumonia. Pooled blood test results revealed lower levels of albumin, calcium, and haemoglobin, and higher CK-MB levels in the coinfected group. Skin lesions in the perianal region were more common among coinfected patients. HIV coinfection is associated with substantially greater clinical severity, greater risks of hospitalization and death, and greater rates of sexually transmitted coinfections among mpox patients. Exploratory subgroup analyses further suggest that suboptimal HIV suppression may be a clinically relevant determinant of adverse outcomes, and that skin lesion severity may depend substantially on host immune status. All subgroup findings are post hoc and hypothesis generating and are limited by the aggregate nature of the data. Clinicians should consider intensified monitoring and comprehensive supportive care for mpox patients with HIV coinfection, particularly those with suboptimal suppression. Strengthening vaccination and health education in high-risk populations and optimizing strategies for ART initiation remain crucial for mitigating the public health impact of MPXV.

title: The epidemiology of the viral hepatitis in Brazil: A scoping review
abstract: BACKGROUND: Brazil has advanced toward eliminating viral hepatitis by 2030 through broad prevention, diagnosis, and treatment policies. Yet substantial gaps persist across the care continuum, especially in vulnerable populations and underserved regions. This scoping review synthesizes nationwide epidemiologic patterns and identifies knowledge gaps to inform policy. METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA‐guided scoping review on seven databases (2013-2024) for Portuguese/Spanish/English observational studies or systematic reviews with post‐2010 data, extracting epidemiological patterns by viral hepatitis type and population group. RESULTS: Across 200 included studies, the combined sample encompassed more than 14.5 million individuals. Hepatitis B was the most studied, followed by hepatitis C. Hepatitis A seroprevalence in general population ranged from 33.3-67.8%. In vulnerable populations, highest seroprevalence was among incarcerated populations (88.1%), followed by immigrants (87.4%) and transgender individuals (75.6%). Hepatitis B presented HBsAg prevalence ranging from 0-7.5% in the general population, with the highest rates in an endemic Amazon region. Hepatitis C seroprevalence varied from 0.04-2.2% in the general population, with higher rates among people who use drugs (36.9%). Hepatitis D was predominantly reported in the Amazon region, with prevalence ranging from 0-23.9%. For hepatitis E, prevalence in the general population ranged from 0.9-59.4%, with the highest value in the South region. CONCLUSIONS: Viral hepatitis in Brazil shows heterogeneous epidemiologic patterns across regions and populations, alongside unequal research output. The predominance of small, cross‐sectional studies and their limited integration with social determinants of health highlight the need for future research employing methodologies that address the gaps identified in this review. The resulting evidence map can guide policies aligned with national elimination goals.
authors: Denize Ornelas Pereira Salvador de Oliveira

title: Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Africa: Epidemiology, Prevention and Outcomes
abstract: Purpose of review: This review synthesizes the current knowledge of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) epidemiology across Northern and sub-Saharan Africa. We examine how causes of HCC differ by region, highlight prevention and early detection strategies, and identify gaps in treatment and palliative care to improve outcomes. Recent findings: The causes of HCC vary markedly across the continent. HCV predominates in Northern Africa, whereas HBV infection and dietary aflatoxin exposure prevail in sub-Saharan Africa. Rising obesity, diabetes, harmful alcohol use, and hepatitis D co-infection are important but under-researched contributors. Most patients still present with advanced disease, fewer than 6% receive curative therapy, median survival is measured in months, and access to palliative care remains dismal. Summary: HCC poses a major challenge in Africa, marked by high incidence, early age at diagnosis, and among the worst survival outcomes worldwide. Primary prevention through HBV birth-dose vaccination, aflatoxin mitigation, and population-level HCV treatment offers the most effective way to reduce mortality, yet implementation barriers persist.

abstract_zh: 综述目的:本综述综合了北非和撒哈拉以南非洲地区肝细胞癌(HCC)流行病学的最新知识。我们研究不同地区肝癌的病因有何不同,强调预防和早期检测策略,并找出治疗和姑息治疗方面的差距,以改善结果。最新发现:整个非洲大陆的肝癌病因差异显着。HCV 在北非占主导地位,而 HBV 感染和膳食黄曲霉毒素暴露在撒哈拉以南非洲占主导地位。肥胖、糖尿病、有害饮酒和丁型肝炎合并感染的增加是重要的原因,但研究不足。大多数患者仍处于晚期疾病,不到 6% 的患者接受了治愈性治疗,中位生存期以月为单位,获得姑息治疗的机会仍然很少。摘要:HCC 在非洲构成了一项重大挑战,其特点是发病率高、诊断年龄早,并且是全球生存结果最差的疾病之一。通过乙型肝炎出生剂量疫苗接种、黄曲霉毒素缓解和人群丙型肝炎治疗进行一级预防是降低死亡率的最有效方法,但实施障碍仍然存在。

title: Early antibiotic exposure reduces progression-free survival in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma patients treated with TACE plus TKI and ICI therapy: a propensity score-matched analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: The combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) and tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) has emerged as a promising treatment strategy for unresectable HCC; however, the impact of concurrent antibiotic use on treatment efficacy remains controversial and poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of early antibiotic (ATB) exposure on the long-term efficacy of TACE, TKI and ICI therapy in patients with unresectable intermediate-to-advanced HCC. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related advanced HCC who received combination therapy with TACE, TKIs, and ICIs at the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University from January 1, 2019, to December 31, 2024. Patients were classified into the ATB group and non-ATB group based on whether they had received ATB therapy within 30 days prior to or 30 days after ICI initiation. The median follow-up duration was 20 months (interquartile range: 12-28 months). Follow-up assessments were performed every 3 months through outpatient reviews, re-admissions, or telephone contact. RESULTS: After PSM, 20 matched pairs were analyzed. No significant difference in overall survival (OS) between the ATB and non-ATB groups (median OS:18.2vs24.0 months; P = 0.692). However, progression-free survival (PFS) was significantly shorter in the ATB group (median PFS:7.6vs12.3 months; P = 0.006). Multivariable analysis revealed that ATB exposure, Child-Pugh class B, and baseline HBV DNA level ≥ 2000 IU/mL were independent predictors of shorter PFS. Subgroup analyses demonstrated that the negative impact of ATB exposure on PFS was more pronounced among patients aged > 60 years, Child-Pugh class B, BCLC stage C, HBV DNA levels between 20 and 2000 IU/mL, and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) ≥ 400 ng/mL. Incidence of adverse events (P = 0.266) did not significantly differ between the ATB and non-ATB groups. CONCLUSION: Early ATB exposure did not affect OS but was independently associated with reduced PFS in unresectable intermediate-to-advanced HCC patients receiving TACE + TKI+ICI. Prophylactic antibiotics should be used cautiously, especially in high-risk subgroups.

title: Real-World Safety and Effectiveness of Cabotegravir in People Living with HIV: Interim Report of a Post-marketing Surveillance in Japan.
abstract: Cabotegravir (CAB) is an integrase strand transfer inhibitor and the first long-acting injectable antiretroviral agent for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), administered with rilpivirine. Because approval in Japan relied largely on overseas and international collaborative trials, domestic real-world evidence remains limited. This study evaluated the real-world safety and effectiveness of CAB in people living with HIV (PLHIV) in Japan. This interim analysis (June 27, 2022 and June 17, 2025) was part of an ongoing post-marketing surveillance of Japanese PLHIV treated with CAB at institutions participating in the HIV-related Drugs Cooperative Survey. Safety was assessed by the incidence of adverse drug reactions (ADRs). Associations between ADR incidence and background characteristics were examined using Fisher’s exact and χ2 tests without multiplicity adjustment. Effectiveness was evaluated using virologic suppression assessed by log-transformed HIV RNA copies/mL and peripheral CD4+ cell counts. A total of 121 and 117 participants were included in the safety and efficacy analysis sets, respectively; most were aged over 20 years, and over 96% were male participants. Overall, 76 ADRs were reported in 45 participants (37.19%). The most frequent ADRs were injection site pain and musculoskeletal pain (12.40% each). Four serious ADRs that were not explicitly deemed unrelated to CAB by the reporting physicians occurred in 4 participants: hepatitis B reactivation, monkeypox, syphilis, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Stratification analyses by participant characteristics revealed high ADR incidences among participants aged ≥ 30 to < 40 years (p = 0.038), without allergy (p = 0.016), and with comorbidities (p = 0.045). HIV RNA copies remained suppressed and CD4+ cell counts were maintained at levels comparable to treatment initiation throughout follow-up. This interim analysis indicates that CAB therapy is safe, with no new safety signals, and effective, as demonstrated by sustained virological suppression and stable CD4+ cell counts. These findings are consistent with outcomes reported in overseas and international collaborative clinical studies. Taking multiple oral medications every day can be challenging for people living with human immunodeficiency virus (PLHIV). Cabotegravir, co-administered with rilpivirine, is the first long-acting injectable HIV treatment that can be given once monthly or every 2 months. Its approval in Japan was primarily based on overseas and international collaborative studies, and real-world clinical evidence in Japan has been limited. To address this gap, a post-marketing surveillance has been conducted to confirm the safety and effectiveness of cabotegravir in Japanese PLHIV. This was a 3-year interim analysis of post-marketing surveillance including 121 participants at 10 institutions in Japan who were virologically suppressed for over 6 months before switching to cabotegravir. During follow-up, 45 participants experienced 76 adverse drug reactions (37.19%) that included injection site pain and musculoskeletal pain (12.40% each), and oral herpes, high cholesterol, thickened or hardened injection site, fever, and decreased white blood cell counts (2.48% each). These findings were consistent with those reported in previous clinical studies. Higher adverse drug reaction rates were observed among participants aged ≥ 30 to < 40 years, those without allergy, and those with other medical conditions. Most adverse drug reactions considered related to cabotegravir occurred within 180 days after treatment initiation. Throughout the follow-up period, HIV RNA copies remained suppressed and CD4+ cell counts were maintained at levels similar to those at treatment initiation. Overall, these results confirm the real-world safety and effectiveness of cabotegravir in Japan.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the real-world safety and effectiveness of cabotegravir, a long-acting injectable integrase strand transfer inhibitor co-administered with rilpivirine, in people living with HIV (PLHIV) in Japan, focusing on post-marketing surveillance outcomes and the central question of its clinical performance in domestic settings.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review reports a 3-year interim analysis of an ongoing post-marketing surveillance conducted in Japan from June 27, 2022 to June 17, 2025, including 121 participants at 10 institutions who were virologically suppressed for over 6 months before switching to cabotegravir. The review describes safety assessment via adverse drug reaction (ADR) incidence and associations with participant characteristics using Fisher’s exact and χ2 tests without multiplicity adjustment, and effectiveness evaluation through virologic suppression (HIV RNA copies/mL) and CD4+ cell counts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that cabotegravir therapy is safe in Japanese PLHIV, with no new safety signals identified, and effective, as evidenced by sustained virologic suppression and stable CD4+ cell counts throughout follow-up. The most frequent ADRs were injection site pain and musculoskeletal pain (12.40% each), and serious ADRs included hepatitis B reactivation, monkeypox, syphilis, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, none explicitly deemed related to cabotegravir by reporting physicians.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights limited domestic real-world evidence for cabotegravir in Japan, as its approval relied largely on overseas and international collaborative trials. Higher ADR incidences were observed among participants aged 30 to <40 years, those without allergy, and those with comorbidities, but these associations were not adjusted for multiplicity and require further validation. The review does not report long-term safety outcomes beyond the interim analysis period.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review implies a need for continued post-marketing surveillance to confirm long-term safety and effectiveness of cabotegravir in Japanese PLHIV, particularly among subgroups with higher ADR incidence. It suggests further investigation into the mechanisms underlying ADR patterns in specific demographic and clinical subgroups, and validation of the observed associations using adjusted statistical methods.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the real-world safety and effectiveness of cabotegravir, a long-acting injectable antiretroviral co-administered with rilpivirine, in people living with HIV (PLHIV) in Japan through a 3-year interim analysis of post-marketing surveillance. The review reports that cabotegravir therapy demonstrated no new safety signals, with sustained virologic suppression and stable CD4+ cell counts, though injection site pain and musculoskeletal pain were common adverse drug reactions. Higher adverse event rates were observed in participants aged 30 to <40 years, those without allergy, and those with comorbidities, but these findings were not adjusted for multiplicity. The review underscores the limited domestic real-world evidence for cabotegravir in Japan, as its approval relied on overseas trials, and calls for continued surveillance and subgroup-specific research to validate these interim findings.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了卡博特韦(一种长效注射整合酶链转移抑制剂与利匹韦林联合给药)在日本艾滋病毒感染者(PLHIV)中的真实安全性和有效性,重点关注上市后监测结果及其在国内环境中临床表现的核心问题。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查报告了对 2022 年 6 月 27 日至 2025 年 6 月 17 日在日本进行的持续上市后监测的 3 年中期分析,包括 10 个机构的 121 名参与者,他们在改用卡博特韦之前已被病毒学抑制了 6 个多月。该综述描述了通过药物不良反应 (ADR) 发生率以及使用 Fisher 精确检验和 χ2 检验与参与者特征的关联(无需多重调整)进行的安全性评估,以及通过病毒学抑制(HIV RNA 拷贝数/mL)和 CD4+ 细胞计数进行的有效性评估。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,卡博特韦疗法对于日本艾滋病病毒感染者是安全的,没有发现新的安全信号,并且在整个随访过程中持续的病毒学抑制和稳定的 CD4+ 细胞计数证明了卡博特韦疗法是有效的。最常见的不良反应是注射部位疼痛和肌肉骨骼疼痛(各 12.40%),严重的不良反应包括乙型肝炎再激活、猴痘、梅毒和 2 型糖尿病,但报告医生没有明确认为与卡博特韦相关。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查强调了卡博特韦在日本国内的实际证据有限,因为其批准主要依赖于海外和国际合作试验。在年龄 30 岁至 <40 岁的参与者、无过敏者和有合并症的参与者中观察到较高的 ADR 发生率,但这些关联未针对多重性进行调整,需要进一步验证。该审查不会报告中期分析期之后的长期安全结果。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查意味着需要持续进行上市后监测,以确认卡博特韦对日本艾滋病毒感染者(尤其是 ADR 发生率较高的亚组)的长期安全性和有效性。它建议进一步研究特定人口和临床亚组中 ADR 模式的潜在机制,并使用调整后的统计方法验证观察到的关联。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了卡博特韦(一种长效注射整合酶链转移抑制剂与利匹韦林联合给药)在日本艾滋病毒感染者(PLHIV)中的真实安全性和有效性,重点关注上市后监测结果及其在国内环境中临床表现的核心问题。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查报告了对 2022 年 6 月 27 日至 2025 年 6 月 17 日在日本进行的持续上市后监测的 3 年中期分析,包括 10 个机构的 121 名参与者,他们在改用卡博特韦之前已被病毒学抑制了 6 个多月。该综述描述了通过药物不良反应 (ADR) 发生率以及使用 Fisher 精确检验和 χ2 检验与参与者特征的关联(无需多重调整)进行的安全性评估,以及通过病毒学抑制(HIV RNA 拷贝数/mL)和 CD4+ 细胞计数进行的有效性评估。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,卡博特韦疗法对于日本艾滋病病毒感染者是安全的,没有发现新的安全信号,并且在整个随访过程中持续的病毒学抑制和稳定的 CD4+ 细胞计数证明了卡博特韦疗法是有效的。最常见的不良反应是注射部位疼痛和肌肉骨骼疼痛(各 12.40%),严重的不良反应包括乙型肝炎再激活、猴痘、梅毒和 2 型糖尿病,但报告医生没有明确认为与卡博特韦相关。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查强调了卡博特韦在日本国内的实际证据有限,因为其批准主要依赖于海外和国际合作试验。在年龄 30 岁至 <40 岁的参与者、无过敏者和有合并症的参与者中观察到较高的 ADR 发生率,但这些关联未针对多重性进行调整,需要进一步验证。该审查不会报告中期分析期之后的长期安全结果。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查意味着需要持续进行上市后监测,以确认卡博特韦对日本艾滋病毒感染者(尤其是 ADR 发生率较高的亚组)的长期安全性和有效性。它建议进一步研究特定人口和临床亚组中 ADR 模式的潜在机制,并使用调整后的统计方法验证观察到的关联。

title: Vaccination status and associated factors among healthcare workers providing primary care: a cross-sectional study in Yaounde, Cameroon
abstract: Abstract Background Healthcare workers (HCWs) are at increased risk of exposure to vaccine-preventable diseases, including hepatitis B, tuberculosis (TB), and tetanus, due to their occupational environment. Despite the availability of safe and effective vaccines, vaccination coverage among HCWs remains suboptimal in many low- and middle-income countries. This study aimed to determine the vaccination coverage for hepatitis B, tuberculosis, and tetanus among HCWs in district hospitals in Yaoundé, Cameroon, and to identify factors associated with incomplete vaccination. Methods A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted from January to June 2024 across all seven district hospitals in Yaoundé. A total of 406 HCWs were enrolled using a structured, self-administered questionnaire. Incomplete vaccination status was defined as nit having received three doses for hepatitis B, at least two doses for TB, and at least three doses for tetanus. Data were analyzed using R Statistics version 4.3.3. Bivariate and multivariate logistic regression models were used to identify predictors of incomplete vaccination, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results Most of participants were female (75.6%) and aged 30-44 years (65.5%). Full vaccination coverage was 36.2% for hepatitis B, 15.8% for tuberculosis, and 53.4% for tetanus. Unvaccinated proportions were 43.1% for hepatitis B, 0.5% for tuberculosis, and 17.2% for tetanus. Multivariate analysis revealed that HCWs aged 55-66 years were significantly less likely to be incompletely vaccinated against hepatitis B compared to those aged 19-29 years (aOR = 0.07; 95% CI: 0.01-0.39; p = 0.004). Nurses and laboratory technicians were more likely to be incompletely vaccinated than doctors (aOR = 7.06; 95% CI: 3.82-13.6; p < 0.001 and aOR = 3.78; 95% CI: 1.73-8.52; p = 0.001, respectively). Longer professional experience was protective against incomplete vaccination for all three vaccines ( p < 0.05). The main barriers to vaccination included high cost, doubts about the need for vaccination, and concerns about side effects. Conclusions Vaccination coverage for hepatitis B, tuberculosis, and tetanus among HCWs in Yaoundé remains suboptimal, particularly for hepatitis B. Addressing financial barriers, improving access to vaccines, and implementing targeted educational interventions are essential to enhance vaccine uptake and protect both HCWs and their patients from preventable occupational infections.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 由于其职业环境,医护人员 (HCW) 接触疫苗可预防疾病的风险增加,包括乙型肝炎、结核病 (TB) 和破伤风。尽管可以获得安全有效的疫苗,但许多低收入和中等收入国家医护人员的疫苗接种覆盖率仍然不够理想。本研究旨在确定喀麦隆雅温得地区医院医护人员的乙型肝炎、结核病和破伤风疫苗接种覆盖率,并确定与疫苗接种不完全相关的因素。方法 2024 年 1 月至 6 月期间,对雅温得所有七家地区医院进行了横断面分析研究。共有 406 名医护人员通过结构化、自填式问卷进行了登记。不完整的疫苗接种状态定义为已接受三剂乙型肝炎疫苗、至少两剂结核病疫苗和至少三剂破伤风疫苗。使用 R Statistics 版本 4.3.3 分析数据。使用双变量和多变量逻辑回归模型来确定不完全疫苗接种的预测因素,统计显着性设置为 p < 0.05。结果 大部分参与者为女性(75.6%),年龄在30-44岁(65.5%)。乙型肝炎、结核病和破伤风疫苗的全面疫苗接种覆盖率分别为 36.2%、15.8% 和 53.4%。乙型肝炎未接种疫苗的比例为 43.1%,结核病未接种疫苗的比例为 0.5%,破伤风疫苗未接种的比例为 17.2%。多变量分析显示,与 19-29 岁的医护人员相比,55-66 岁的医护人员未完全接种乙型肝炎疫苗的可能性明显较低(aOR = 0.07;95% CI:0.01-0.39;p = 0.004)。护士和实验室技术人员比医生更有可能未完全接种疫苗(分别为 aOR = 7.06;95% CI:3.82-13.6;p < 0.001;aOR = 3.78;95% CI:1.73-8.52;p = 0.001)。较长的专业经验可以防止所有三种疫苗的疫苗接种不完全(p < 0.05)。疫苗接种的主要障碍包括成本高、对疫苗接种必要性的怀疑以及对副作用的担忧。结论 雅温得医护人员的乙型肝炎、结核病和破伤风疫苗接种覆盖率仍然不够理想,尤其是乙型肝炎。解决经济障碍、改善疫苗的获取以及实施有针对性的教育干预措施对于提高疫苗接种率并保护医护人员及其患者免受可预防的职业感染至关重要。

title: Monitoring of the Cascade of Care in Patients With Chronic HBV in Primary Care Clinics in Australia.
abstract: To achieve hepatitis B virus (HBV) elimination in Australia, a shift from hospital to community-based care is needed. This study aimed to describe the prevalence of chronic HBV and uptake of the cascade of care in primary care patients. This prospective cohort study was conducted in 76 urban and regional primary care clinics across Victoria, Australia between 1/7/2020 and 30/6/2023. Anonymised socio-demographic, clinical and laboratory data from general practice (GP) clinics' electronic medical records (EMR) were extracted. Descriptive analysis of the cohort of clinic clients with HBV was performed. A total of 346,927 individuals attended appointments across the study period. Of these, 25,212 had records indicating HBV-related testing. 491 (0.14%) individuals had evidence of current HBV infection defined as HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) positive and/or HBV DNA positive. 469 attended the clinics during the study period, among whom 239 (51%) were female. In the GP EMR, only 59 (13%) had evidence of at least one HBV DNA test and at least one ALT test ordered. Fourteen patients (3%) had record of being reviewed for HBV management by the clinic nurse or GP and 78 (17%) reviewed by a viral hepatitis specialist. Ninety-two (20%) were on treatment for HBV. Of people receiving treatment, 23 (25%) had a record of linkage to specialist care. Our data show that significant gaps in the cascade of care remain for people with chronic HBV in primary care settings, with a low proportion of patients having evidence of participating in all stages of the HBV cascade of care.

title: High-resolution mapping of chromatin conformation in HBeAg-treated macrophage provides insights into pathogenesis of HBV-related liver diseases
abstract: Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) e antigen (HBeAg) plays a critical role in inducing macrophage activation and subsequent immune tolerance, which facilitates viral immune escape. However, the underlying spatial 3D genomic and epigenetic mechanisms driving this macrophage dysfunction remain largely unknown. Methods To map the topological and transcriptional regulatory landscape, we integrated RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq), high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C), and chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing (ChIP-seq) to comprehensively analyze control and HBeAg-stimulated macrophages. Key findings were cross-validated using human HBV-infected datasets. Result HBeAg robustly activated pro-inflammatory transcriptional programs, prominently featuring the TNF signaling pathway as a central node. Hi-C analysis revealed profound global 3D chromatin reorganization accompanying this phenotypic shift. Specifically, inactive-to-active (B-to-A) compartment switching, coupled with de novo H3K27ac enhancer accumulation, directly drove the upregulation of functional genes such as MET and FHOD3. Furthermore, topologically associating domain (TAD) restructuring, particularly TAD merging, exposed new regulatory elements to upregulate FLNB and SESN2. Conversely, the disruption of specific intrachromosomal loops resulted in the targeted downregulation of genes like KBTBD11 and BLVRB. Mechanistically, targeted epigenetic reprogramming drove this 3D structural rewiring: H3K27ac enhancer deposition was enriched for AP-1/STAT motifs, CTCF coordinated with FOX-family factors to alter structural boundaries, and HLTF mediated targeted H3K27me3-associated gene silencing. Conclusion HBeAg orchestrates a highly coordinated hierarchical restructuring of the 3D genome and targeted epigenetic reprogramming to induce macrophage dysfunction. The identified structural variants and core spatial-target genes (such as MET, FLNB, and BLVRB) provide novel mechanistic insights and represent potential therapeutic targets for HBV-related liver diseases.

Methods To map the topological and transcriptional regulatory landscape, we integrated RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq), high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C), and chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing (ChIP-seq) to comprehensively analyze control and HBeAg-stimulated macrophages. Key findings were cross-validated using human HBV-infected datasets. Result HBeAg robustly activated pro-inflammatory transcriptional programs, prominently featuring the TNF signaling pathway as a central node. Hi-C analysis revealed profound global 3D chromatin reorganization accompanying this phenotypic shift. Specifically, inactive-to-active (B-to-A) compartment switching, coupled with de novo H3K27ac enhancer accumulation, directly drove the upregulation of functional genes such as MET and FHOD3. Furthermore, topologically associating domain (TAD) restructuring, particularly TAD merging, exposed new regulatory elements to upregulate FLNB and SESN2. Conversely, the disruption of specific intrachromosomal loops resulted in the targeted downregulation of genes like KBTBD11 and BLVRB. Mechanistically, targeted epigenetic reprogramming drove this 3D structural rewiring: H3K27ac enhancer deposition was enriched for AP-1/STAT motifs, CTCF coordinated with FOX-family factors to alter structural boundaries, and HLTF mediated targeted H3K27me3-associated gene silencing. Conclusion HBeAg orchestrates a highly coordinated hierarchical restructuring of the 3D genome and targeted epigenetic reprogramming to induce macrophage dysfunction. The identified structural variants and core spatial-target genes (such as MET, FLNB, and BLVRB) provide novel mechanistic insights and represent potential therapeutic targets for HBV-related liver diseases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses why Hepatitis B virus (HBV) e antigen (HBeAg) induces macrophage activation and immune tolerance, a process linked to viral immune escape, while the spatial 3D genomic and epigenetic mechanisms underlying macrophage dysfunction remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study integrated RNA-sequencing, high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C), and chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing (ChIP-seq) to analyze control and HBeAg-stimulated macrophages, with key findings cross-validated using human HBV-infected datasets.
analysis.methods: RNA-sequencing, Hi-C, and ChIP-sequencing were used to map the topological and transcriptional regulatory landscape in macrophages exposed to HBeAg, including analyses of chromatin compartment switching, enhancer accumulation, topologically associating domain (TAD) restructuring, and epigenetic reprogramming.
analysis.main_results: HBeAg robustly activated pro-inflammatory transcriptional programs, particularly the TNF signaling pathway, accompanied by global 3D chromatin reorganization, including inactive-to-active compartment switching, de novo H3K27ac enhancer accumulation, TAD merging, and targeted intrachromosomal loop disruption affecting genes such as MET, FHOD3, FLNB, SESN2, KBTBD11, and BLVRB.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that HBeAg orchestrates a coordinated hierarchical restructuring of the 3D genome and targeted epigenetic reprogramming to induce macrophage dysfunction, identifying structural variants and core spatial-target genes (e.g., MET, FLNB, BLVRB) as novel mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting the identified epigenetic and structural mechanisms or the implicated genes may offer therapeutic strategies for HBV-related liver diseases by modulating macrophage dysfunction and immune tolerance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro macrophage models and cross-validation with human HBV-infected datasets, leaving uncertainty about the direct applicability of these mechanisms in vivo and the clinical relevance of the identified targets.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how Hepatitis B virus e antigen (HBeAg) drives macrophage activation and immune tolerance, a process implicated in viral immune escape, by mapping the 3D genomic and epigenetic changes in macrophages. Using RNA-sequencing, Hi-C, and ChIP-sequencing, the authors demonstrate that HBeAg induces global chromatin reorganization, including compartment switching, enhancer accumulation, and topologically associating domain restructuring, alongside targeted epigenetic reprogramming. These changes activate pro-inflammatory pathways such as TNF signaling while upregulating genes like MET and FLNB and downregulating genes like BLVRB. The study proposes that this coordinated 3D genome restructuring and epigenetic reprogramming underlies macrophage dysfunction, offering potential therapeutic targets for HBV-related liver diseases. However, the findings are derived from in vitro models and require validation in vivo to confirm their clinical relevance.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解释了为什么乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) e 抗原 (HBeAg) 会诱导巨噬细胞激活和免疫耐受,这一过程与病毒免疫逃逸有关,而巨噬细胞功能障碍背后的空间 3D 基因组和表观遗传机制仍知之甚少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究整合了 RNA 测序、高通量染色体构象捕获 (Hi-C) 和染色质免疫沉淀测序 (ChIP-seq) 来分析对照和 HBeAg 刺激的巨噬细胞,并使用人类 HBV 感染数据集对关键发现进行了交叉验证。
elements_zh.methods: RNA 测序、Hi-C 和 ChIP 测序用于绘制暴露于 HBeAg 的巨噬细胞的拓扑和转录调控图谱,包括染色质区室转换、增强子积累、拓扑关联域 (TAD) 重组和表观遗传重编程的分析。
elements_zh.main_results: HBeAg 强烈激活促炎转录程序,特别是 TNF 信号通路,伴随着全局 3D 染色质重组,包括非活性到活性区室转换、从头 H3K27ac 增强子积累、TAD 合并以及影响 MET、FHOD3、FLNB、SESN2、KBBTD11 和 BLVRB 等基因的靶向染色体内环破坏。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,HBeAg 协调协调 3D 基因组的层次结构重组和有针对性的表观遗传重编程,以诱导巨噬细胞功能障碍,识别结构变异和核心空间目标基因(例如 MET、FLNB、BLVRB)作为新的机制见解和潜在的治疗靶点。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,针对已确定的表观遗传和结构机制或相关基因可能通过调节巨噬细胞功能障碍和免疫耐受为 HBV 相关肝病提供治疗策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于体外巨噬细胞模型以及与人类 HBV 感染数据集的交叉验证,这使得这些机制在体内的直接适用性以及已确定目标的临床相关性存在不确定性。

abstract_zh: 背景乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)e抗原(HBeAg)在诱导巨噬细胞激活和随后的免疫耐受中发挥着关键作用,从而促进病毒免疫逃逸。然而,驱动这种巨噬细胞功能障碍的潜在空间 3D 基因组和表观遗传机制仍然很大程度上未知。方法 为了绘制拓扑和转录调控图谱,我们集成了 RNA 测序 (RNA-seq)、高通量染色体构象捕获 (Hi-C) 和染色质免疫沉淀测序 (ChIP-seq),以全面分析对照和 HBeAg 刺激的巨噬细胞。使用人类 HBV 感染数据集对主要发现进行了交叉验证。结果 HBeAg 强烈激活促炎转录程序,突出以 TNF 信号通路为中心节点。Hi-C 分析揭示了伴随这种表型转变的深刻的全局 3D 染色质重组。具体来说,非活性到活性(B 到 A)区室的转换,加上 H3K27ac 增强子的从头积累,直接驱动了 MET 和 FHOD3 等功能基因的上调。此外,拓扑关联域(TAD)重组,特别是 TAD 合并,暴露了新的调控元件来上调 FLNB 和 SESN2。相反,特定染色体内环的破坏导致 KBTBD11 和 BLVRB 等基因的定向下调。从机制上讲,靶向表观遗传重编程驱动了这种 3D 结构重新布线:AP-1/STAT 基序的 H3K27ac 增强子沉积富集,CTCF 与 FOX 家族因子协调改变结构边界,HLTF 介导靶向 H3K27me3 相关基因沉默。结论 HBeAg 协调 3D 基因组的高度协调的层次结构重组和有针对性的表观遗传重编程以诱导巨噬细胞功能障碍。已确定的结构变异和核心空间靶基因(如 MET、FLNB 和 BLVRB)提供了新的机制见解,并代表了 HBV 相关肝病的潜在治疗靶点。

title: HBV-Specific T Cell Responses for Short-Term Hepatitis Progression Prediction: A Comparative, Interpretable Machine Learning Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: As central determinants of viral control and immunopathology, hepatitis B virus (HBV)-specific T-cell responses provide more clinically meaningful information than routine biochemical and virological markers. Nevertheless, most existing prediction models rely primarily on clinical parameters and rarely incorporate HBV-specific T-cell responses, potentially limiting their predictive performance and biological interpretability. To develop an accurate and interpretable model for predicting hepatitis progression, we evaluated diverse machine learning (ML) methods integrating multisource data. METHODS: We enrolled a cohort of 479 patients and divided them into training and testing cohorts based on admission time. Clinical data, treatment regimens, and HBV-specific T-cell immune responses were collected. A comprehensive benchmarking of 10 ML models was conducted through 5-fold cross-validation on the training cohort across varying feature combinations and algorithmic performances. The ML models were independently evaluated on the testing cohort, and significant predictive factors were identified. RESULTS: Based on alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels at 6- and 12-month follow-ups, the patients were stratified into hepatitis (ALT > 40 U/L) and non-hepatitis (ALT ≤ 40 U/L) groups. The predictive performance was significantly improved after integrating clinical indicator features (CIF) and HBV-specific T-cell features (STCF). An XGBoost model based on six selected features (three CIF and three STCF) demonstrated especially robust performance, achieving AUCs of 0.874 (validation) and 0.880 (testing) at 6 months follow up and 0.851 (validation) and 0.845 (testing) at 12 months. To facilitate clinical application, a web-based tool was developed for personalized risk assessment. CONCLUSIONS: Incorporating HBV-specific T-cell responses into the predictive framework improves the prediction of disease progression among HBV-infected individuals. The developed interpretable model is a potentially valuable tool for early risk stratification, facilitating proactive monitoring.

title: HBV, HCV and HIV Infections among Pregnant Women Attending Antenatal Care at the Health Facilities in Ekiti South, Nigeria
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) are blood-borne infections with the potential for mother-to-child transmission and remain important concerns in antenatal care in sub-Saharan Africa. This cross-sectional study determined the seroprevalence of HBV, HCV, and HIV among pregnant women attending selected health facilities in Ekiti South Senatorial District, Nigeria. A total of 710 pregnant women were recruited from six Local Government Areas: Ekiti South West, Ikere, Ise, Emure, Ekiti East, and Gbonyin. Sociodemographic data and information on knowledge, awareness, and attitudes were collected using a structured questionnaire. Venous blood specimens were obtained aseptically and screened for hepatitis B surface antigen, anti-HCV antibodies, and HIV antibodies. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to assess prevalence and associations at p < 0.05. The overall seroprevalence was 2.5% (18/710) for HBV, 1.5% (11/710) for HIV, and 0% for HCV. No co-infection was detected. Age group was significantly associated with HIV infection (p < 0.001), whereas location, marital status, residence, gestational age, education, and occupation were not significantly associated with HIV status. HBsAg positivity was not significantly associated with any assessed sociodemographic variable. The findings indicate an intermediate level of HBV endemicity in the study population and support sustained antenatal screening, linkage to care, health education, HBV vaccination, and prevention of mother-to-child transmission services.

title: Contemporary global epidemiology of cirrhosis
abstract: Cirrhosis remains a major global cause of morbidity and mortality, with rapidly evolving etiologic drivers. This review summarizes the contemporary global epidemiology of cirrhosis, highlighting regional patterns and major transitions in underlying causes to inform prevention and policy. In 2021, cirrhosis and chronic liver disease accounted for ~1.4 million deaths worldwide. Although age-standardized mortality rates have declined in many regions, the absolute burden continues to rise due to population growth and aging. Reductions in hepatitis B and C–related cirrhosis, driven by vaccination, screening, and antiviral therapy, have been offset by a growing contribution from steatotic liver disease. High–sociodemographic index (SDI) regions exhibit lower mortality but increasing prevalence, reflecting improved survival and expanding metabolic risk, whereas low- and lower-middle–SDI regions continue to experience high mortality. Addressing the global burden of cirrhosis will require sustained public health investment focused on viral hepatitis elimination, alcohol-associated harm reduction, metabolic risk management, and equitable access to early detection and care.

title: Development and validation of a novel prognostic score for HBV-related acute-on-chronic liver failure
abstract: Background Acute-on-chronic liver failure patients have high short-term mortality rates, and HBV infection is the most common cause. Current prognostic models for HBV-ACLF patients have limitations. Thus, the development of an ideal model remains an important unsolved problem. Aims To develop a new model and validate its prognostic predictive capacity. Methods Among 5854 liver failure patients admitted to the Second Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University from 2008 to 2023, 1170 HBV-ACLF cases were finally enrolled, which were randomly divided into a development cohort ( n = 822) or validation cohort ( n = 348). First, we obtained important predictive factors about 28-day and 90-day mortality using cox regression analysis and developed new prognostic scores. Second, the new scores were compared with current models through ROC curves, calibration curves and DCA curves. Third, using survival analysis, the new scores were risk-stratified according to optimal cut-off values. Results The AHF-MELD and AHN-MELD scores’ predictive capacity were stronger than MELD, MELD-sodium, CLIF-C OF and AARC scores and comparable to CLIF-C ACLF, COSSH ACLF and COSSH ACLF II scores. There was no significant difference between the observed and the predicted 28-day and 90-day mortality probabilities of new scores. The AHF-MELD and AHN-MELD scores have positive net benefits over a wide range of threshold probabilities and outperform conventional scores. The 28-day and 90-day survival rates were significantly lower in high-risk groups than in low-risk groups. Conclusion The AHF-MELD and AHN-MELD scores may serve as potential predictive tools for the short-term prognosis of HBV-ACLF patients. Our study may provide useful information for clinicians managing these patients.

title: Ancient whole genomes reveal regional selection during adaptation to Neolithic lifestyle in Western Eurasia
abstract: The introduction of agriculture in Western Eurasia during the Mesolithic-Neolithic transition reshaped human lifestyle, demography and pathogen exposure. Yet, the associated selective pressures remain incompletely resolved because previous ancient DNA studies relied on targeted SNP panels and yielded non-overlapping results. Here, using high-coverage whole-genome data from 152 ancient individuals, including 12 newly sequenced genomes from the Iron Gates, we show that adaptation during this transition was geographically structured and involved selection of both Early Farmer and Hunter-Gatherer alleles. By combining scans of population differentiation, extended haplotype homozygosity, and adaptive admixture, we identify candidate loci under selection in ancestral and admixed populations. Extending the analysis beyond SNPs, we also detect differential copy-number variants, ancestry-associated shifts in transposable-element abundance, and an early Neolithic hepatitis B infection. Functional analyses including effects on gene expression suggested selection on immune, metabolic, reproductive, sensory, and behavioural processes. Taken together, our results reveal a broader and more regionally variable adaptive landscape than previously appreciated.

title: Supramolecular Self-Assembly of Lycorine with Glycyrrhizic Acid into a Nanodrug for Safe and Sustained Anti-HBV Therapy
abstract: Achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B remains a major challenge, as conventional therapies struggle to eliminate the hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and subsequently restore adaptive antiviral immunity. Lycorine (LY), a compound with broad-spectrum antiviral activity, has shown particular promise inhibiting HBsAg secretion. However, its clinical application is severely limited by significant cytotoxicity, the induction of apoptosis, a short half-life, and adverse in vivo effects. To overcome these barriers and enhance its therapeutic potential, we designed a self-assembled nanomedicine (LGN) by co-assembling LY with glycyrrhizic acid, a natural anti-HBV agent. This strategy not only protected LY from premature degradation and enabled its sustained release in the colon but also markedly attenuated LY-induced systemic toxicity. Notably, LGN effectively suppressed HBsAg secretion (IC50 = 2.15 ± 0.09 μM) with a selectivity index (SI > 93) over two-fold higher than that of LY alone (SI = 39.26). Furthermore, LGN concurrently inhibited HBV DNA replication, pgRNA transcription, and the expression of viral protein HBc and HBx, indicating a multitargeted, host-dependent mechanism distinct from nucleos(t)ide analogs. Treatment with this nanomedicine in the HDI model further demonstrated its therapeutic potential against HBV with apparent safety. Further transcriptomic study confirmed that LGN induces a distinct host transcriptional program that disrupts multiple critical stages of the HBV life cycle including viral entry, covalently closed circular DNA maintenance, gene transcription, and immune evasion. Collectively, these findings provide valuable insights into exploiting natural products like LY for antiviral therapy and underscore the potential of self-assembly technology in improving drug safety and pharmacokinetic profiles.

title: Congenital generalized lipodystrophy Type 2 (BSCL2; OMIM #269700) presenting with muscular hypertrophy and chronic steatorrhea in a Pakistani child: a pediatric case report confirmed by real-time PCR gene analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Congenital generalized lipodystrophy (CGL), or Berardinelli-Seip syndrome, is a rare autosomal recessive condition with near-complete lack of metabolically functional adipocytes since birth or in early infancy, leading to severe metabolic complications. The prevalence of CGL is less than 1 case per million births, and it occurs in four genetic types (CGL1-CGL4). CGL type 2 (mutations in the BSCL2 gene; OMIM #269700) is the most common subtype (70–80% of cases), and has the most severe metabolic complications. Timely diagnosis is essential to avoid potentially fatal complications by early metabolic surveillance and treatment. Case presentation A 5.5-year-old Pakistani male child was referred for a muscular bodybuilder-like look since 24 months of age, chronic steatorrhea (4–5 times a day, aggravated by fat intake), hyperphagia, and poor growth. His birth was normal at term through a normal vaginal delivery and with normal weight and milestones. His family history was negative for lipodystrophy and metabolic disease. His weight (16 kg) and height (105 cm) were below 10th percentile with a BMI of 14.5 kg/m2 (< 5th percentile). He had diffuse muscular hypertrophy with a complete loss of subcutaneous fat, visible veins, coarse face with facial lipoatrophy, abdominal distension with hepatomegaly (4 cm below the right costal margin, span 12 cm) and an everted umbilicus. There were no signs of acanthosis nigricans, xanthomas, hirsutism or splenomegaly. Real-Time PCR (RT-PCR) gene analysis confirmed CGL Type 2: BSCL2 exons 4 and 7 were detected; AGPAT2, CAV1, and PTRF were not detected. Both parents confirmed as carriers; all four siblings are unaffected (three heterozygous carriers, one non-carrier). Routine investigations showed macrocytic anaemia (Hb 10 g/dL, MCV 110.8 fL), raised transaminases (ALT 71 U/L, AST 97 U/L), grossly raised IgG (2727.98 mg/dL) and low IgA (4.39 mg/dL). Ultrasonography showed hepatic steatosis. Creatine phosphokinase (103 U/L) was normal, ruling out primary muscular dystrophy. IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase was negative, so coeliac disease was excluded. Hepatitis B, C and HIV were negative. Rickets and skeletal dysplasia were ruled out by a skeletal survey. Fasting triglycerides 862 mg/dL, serum leptin 0.4 ng/mL, and HOMA-IR 10.4 confirmed severe metabolic dysfunction characteristic of CGL2. Based on clinical and biochemical findings, RT-PCR confirmed the diagnosis of CGL type 2 (BSCL2; OMIM #269700) was made. A low-fat diet (20–30% of total energy) with medium-chain triglyceride supplementation, metabolic control and genetic counselling was started. Conclusions This RT-PCR confirmed case of CGL2 demonstrates the triad of CGL: diffuse lipoatrophy with muscular hypertrophy, hepatomegaly secondary to steatosis, and steatorrhoea, with poor growth. To our knowledge, this is the first RT-PCR confirmed CGL2 case reported from Pakistan. Early diagnosis of this rare condition is important to start life-changing metabolic interventions that include dietary restriction, metreleptin replacement and treatment of dyslipidaemia, which may dramatically impact the disease progression and outcome in childhood.

title: AURKA regulates HBV-induced hepatic stellate cell inflammation and liver fibrosis by modulating K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of TLR3
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB), caused by persistent hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, continues to pose a major global health threat. Aurora kinase A (AURKA) has been implicated in fibrosis, yet its role in HBV-induced liver fibrosis remains unclear. This study investigated the function and mechanism of AURKA in hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation and fibrogenesis during CHB. Bioinformatics screening of GSE83148 dataset and validation in human CHB liver specimens, LX-2 HSCs treated with conditioned medium (CM) from HBV-replicating cells, and a persistent HBV recombinant cccDNA (rcccDNA) mouse model established by tail-vein injection of Ad/rcccDNA were performed. Gene and protein expression was analyzed by quantitative PCR and immunoblotting, respectively. Cytokine levels were measured by ELISA. Mitochondrial function was assessed via ROS and JC-1 assays. Protein interactions and ubiquitination were evaluated by co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and protein stability assays. In additional experiments, LX-2 cells were stimulated with purified HBV virions at varying MOIs to assess direct viral effects. AURKA was significantly upregulated in CHB patients and HBV-CM-treated LX-2 HSCs. In LX-2 HSCs, AURKA knockdown attenuated HBV-CM-induced inflammatory cytokine secretion (IL‐1β, IL‐6), mitochondrial dysfunction (mitochondrial ROS, mitochondrial membrane potential), HSC proliferation, and fibrotic marker expression (COL I, α-SMA). Mechanistically, AURKA interacted with TLR3 and was associated with its K48-linked polyubiquitination and degradation. TLR3 silencing abolished the protective effects of AURKA knockdown. In vivo, using a persistent HBV rcccDNA mouse model, AURKA knockdown ameliorated HBV-induced hepatic inflammation and fibrosis by upregulating TLR3. Notably, purified HBV virions alone were sufficient to dose-dependently induce AURKA expression and downstream fibrotic responses in HSCs. This study identifies a novel AURKA/TLR3 axis that regulates HBV-induced HSC activation and liver fibrosis, positioning AURKA as a potential therapeutic target for CHB-associated fibrosis.

source_records.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB), caused by persistent hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, continues to pose a major global health threat. Aurora kinase A (AURKA) has been implicated in fibrosis, yet its role in HBV-induced liver fibrosis remains unclear. This study investigated the function and mechanism of AURKA in hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation and fibrogenesis during CHB. Bioinformatics screening of GSE83148 dataset and validation in human CHB liver specimens, LX-2 HSCs treated with conditioned medium (CM) from HBV-replicating cells, and a persistent HBV recombinant cccDNA (rcccDNA) mouse model established by tail-vein injection of Ad/rcccDNA were performed. Gene and protein expression was analyzed by quantitative PCR and immunoblotting, respectively. Cytokine levels were measured by ELISA. Mitochondrial function was assessed via ROS and JC-1 assays. Protein interactions and ubiquitination were evaluated by co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and protein stability assays. In additional experiments, LX-2 cells were stimulated with purified HBV virions at varying MOIs to assess direct viral effects. AURKA was significantly upregulated in CHB patients and HBV-CM-treated LX-2 HSCs. In LX-2 HSCs, AURKA knockdown attenuated HBV-CM-induced inflammatory cytokine secretion (IL‐1β, IL‐6), mitochondrial dysfunction (mitochondrial ROS, mitochondrial membrane potential), HSC proliferation, and fibrotic marker expression (COL I, α-SMA). Mechanistically, AURKA interacted with TLR3 and was associated with its K48-linked polyubiquitination and degradation. TLR3 silencing abolished the protective effects of AURKA knockdown. In vivo, using a persistent HBV rcccDNA mouse model, AURKA knockdown ameliorated HBV-induced hepatic inflammation and fibrosis by upregulating TLR3. Notably, purified HBV virions alone were sufficient to dose-dependently induce AURKA expression and downstream fibrotic responses in HSCs. This study identifies a novel AURKA/TLR3 axis that regulates HBV-induced HSC activation and liver fibrosis, positioning AURKA as a potential therapeutic target for CHB-associated fibrosis.

abstract_zh: 由持续乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染引起的慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)继续对全球健康构成重大威胁。极光激酶 A (AURKA) 与纤维化有关,但其在 HBV 诱导的肝纤维化中的作用仍不清楚。本研究探讨了 AURKA 在 CHB 期间肝星状细胞 (HSC) 激活和纤维形成中的功能和机制。对 GSE83148 数据集进行生物信息学筛选,并在人 CHB 肝脏标本、用来自 HBV 复制细胞的条件培养基 (CM) 处理的 LX-2 HSC 以及通过尾静脉注射 Ad/rcccDNA 建立的持久性 HBV 重组 cccDNA (rcccDNA) 小鼠模型中进行验证。分别通过定量PCR和免疫印迹分析基因和蛋白质表达。通过ELISA测量细胞因子水平。通过 ROS 和 JC-1 测定评估线粒体功能。通过免疫共沉淀 (Co-IP) 和蛋白质稳定性测定评估蛋白质相互作用和泛素化。在其他实验中,用纯化的 HBV 病毒粒子以不同的 MOI 刺激 LX-2 细胞,以评估直接病毒效应。AURKA 在 CHB 患者和 HBV-CM 治疗的 LX-2 HSC 中显着上调。在 LX-2 HSC 中,AURKA 敲低减弱了 HBV-CM 诱导的炎症细胞因子分泌(IL-1β、IL-6)、线粒体功能障碍(线粒体 ROS、线粒体膜电位)、HSC 增殖和纤维化标志物表达(COL I、α-SMA)。从机制上讲,AURKA 与 TLR3 相互作用,并与其 K48 连接的多聚泛素化和降解相关。TLR3 沉默消除了 AURKA 敲低的保护作用。在体内,使用持续性 HBV rcccDNA 小鼠模型,AURKA 敲低通过上调 TLR3 改善 HBV 诱导的肝脏炎症和纤维化。值得注意的是,单独纯化的 HBV 病毒体足以剂量依赖性地诱导 HSC 中的 AURKA 表达和下游纤维化反应。这项研究确定了一个新的 AURKA/TLR3 轴,可以调节 HBV 诱导的 HSC 激活和肝纤维化,将 AURKA 定位为 CHB 相关纤维化的潜在治疗靶点。

title: Potential Risks and Benefits of Low-Barrier Access and Monitoring for HIV Preexposure Prophylaxis: A Modeling Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: PrEP prevents HIV acquisition, but its population-level impact is limited by access barriers. Low-barrier delivery of daily oral tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine (TDF/FTC), such as over-the-counter (OTC) availability, could improve access by eliminating clinic visits, though reduced monitoring may increase risks including drug resistance, renal toxicity, and hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation. We estimated the benefits and risks of OTC PrEP. METHODS: Using a stochastic network-based model of HIV/STI transmission among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) in Atlanta, we simulated two delivery pathways: clinic-based PrEP and OTC PrEP with simplified initiation and reduced monitoring. We modeled 10-50% increases in PrEP coverage over 10 years. Outcomes included HIV infections averted, STI incidence, contraindicated PrEP use (GFR 90% without reducing prevention benefits, and frequent renal monitoring reduced renal risk. CONCLUSIONS: OTC PrEP could produce population-level HIV prevention benefits if it expands coverage beyond clinic-based care. However, its net public health impact depends on implementation choices that preserve safety functions, particularly HIV testing at initiation and renal monitoring, without undermining access gains.

abstract_zh: 背景:PrEP 可防止 HIV 感染,但其对人群的影响因获取障碍而受到限制。每日口服富马酸替诺福韦二吡呋酯/恩曲他滨 (TDF/FTC) 的低门槛给药,例如非处方药 (OTC),可以通过消除门诊就诊来改善可及性,但减少监测可能会增加风险,包括耐药性、肾毒性和乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 重新激活。我们评估了 OTC PrEP 的益处和风险。方法:使用亚特兰大同性恋、双性恋和其他男男性行为者 (GBMSM) 中 HIV/STI 传播的随机网络模型,我们模拟了两种传递途径:基于诊所的 PrEP 和 OTC PrEP,简化了启动并减少了监测。我们模拟了 10 年内 PrEP 覆盖率增加 10-50% 的情况。成果包括避免 HIV 感染、性传播感染发病率、禁忌使用 PrEP(GFR 90% 且不会降低预防效益,以及频繁的肾脏监测可降低肾脏风险)。结论:非处方药 PrEP 如果将覆盖范围扩大到临床护理之外,可以产生人群层面的 HIV 预防效益。然而,其净公共健康影响取决于在不损害获得收益的情况下保留安全功能的实施选择,特别是初始 HIV 检测和肾脏监测。
